嘉靖十四年進士登科錄

玉音

嘉靖十四年三月初九日，少保兼太子太保、禮部尚書、翰林院學士臣夏言等於奉天門奏為科舉事：「會試天下舉人，取中三百二十五名。本年四月初二日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，少保兼太子太保、吏部尚書、武英殿大學士李時等五十八員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

光祿大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太保、吏部尚書、武英殿大學士李時〔壬戌進士〕。
光祿大夫、柱國、太子太保、吏部尚書兼兵部尚書汪鋐〔壬戌進士〕。
資政大夫、正治上卿、戶部尚書梁材〔己未進士〕。
資政大夫、刑部尚書聶賢〔庚戌進士〕。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Fourteenth Year of Jiajing (1535)

Imperial Pronouncement

On the ninth day of the third month of the fourteenth year of Jiajing, your servant Xia Yan, Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and others memorialized at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations:

“The Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm has selected 325 successful candidates. For the Palace Examination on the second day of the fourth month of this year, we request the appointment of 58 officials as Readers and other officiating personnel, including Li Shi, Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall. The distinctions of status conferred upon the metropolitan graduates shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao. The first class shall, according to precedent, comprise three men: the first shall receive rank 6b, and the second and third rank 7a, with the designation ‘metropolitan graduate with honors.’ Those in the second class shall receive rank 7b and the designation ‘metropolitan graduate.’ Those in the third class shall receive rank 8a and the designation ‘equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’”

The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respect this.

Readers

Li Shi was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.〕

Wang Hong was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel, concurrently Minister of War. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.〕

Liang Cai was Grand Master for Aid in Governance, Senior Minister for Orthodox Governance, and Minister of Revenue. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year.〕

Nie Xian was Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Justice. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the gengxu year.〕

Gu Dingchen, Grand Master of Rectitude and Governor for Aid in Governance, administered the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent and served as Left Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently as Academician of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Xie Pi, Grand Master of Exemplary Service and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently served as Expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Zhang Bi, Grand Master of Straightforward Service and Academician Expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Liao Daonan, Grand Master for Meritorious Service and Academician Lecturer of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

Cai Ang, Grand Master for Meritorious Service and Academician Lecturer of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Xia Yan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Junior Guardian and concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Huang Wan, Grand Master of Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Rites, was a student admitted by virtue of an official’s status.

Huang Zongming, Grand Master of Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors
On the morning of the second day of the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Jiajing (1535), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.
On the morning of the sixth day of the fourth month, all civil and military officials attended in their court robes, standing in their assigned ranks. That day, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard arranged the ceremonial regalia at the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites bore the yellow announcement of successful candidates out through Chang’an Left Gate, led by drums and music, and posted it outside. Officials of Shuntian Prefecture then escorted the first-ranked graduate (zhuangyuan) to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.
On the seventh day of the fourth month…

translation_en:
…an imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates proceeded to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the rites.
On the ninth day of the fourth month, court robes, a cap, and a girdle were bestowed upon the first-ranked graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the tenth day of the fourth month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial of gratitude for imperial favor.
On the eleventh day of the fourth month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names upon it.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Han Yinglong was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student at a government school, he specialized in the Book of Rites (Liji). His courtesy name was Ruhua, and he ranked fiftieth in family order. He was thirty-eight years old, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengxia, his grandfather Guang, and his father Xian; his mother was née Shen. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Ronghua (an official awaiting selection for appointment), Yingfu, and Yinggui; his younger brothers were Yingkui and Yingyuan. He married a woman née Fu. He placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Sheng held official household registration in the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes (Yijing). His courtesy name was Zhigao, and he ranked fiftieth in family order. He was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather Menghong was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites. His grandfather Xin was granted the title Secretary in the Ministry of Justice and posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites. His father Sui, Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-chief, was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites and the posthumous name Zhonglie. His mother, née Yang, received successive patents of honor as Lady. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Ji (Chief Official), Xi (Registrar), Kan (Resident Commandant in the regimental camps, acting as Assistant Regional Military Commissioner), Chi (Assistant Director of the Seals Office), Jie (a student of the Directorate of Education), Tang 堂, Tang 塘, Dian 壂, and Dian 坫; his younger brother was Jun 埈. He married a woman née Han and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shan was registered in a military household in Gao'an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Yuejing, and he ranked fifth in family order. He was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Ziji, and his father Wenxuan; his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were still living. His elder brother was Yueli; his younger brothers were Yuejian and Yuewei. He married a woman née Huang. He placed thirty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: ninety-five men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Li Ji, registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangzai; he ranked sixth in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiyu, his grandfather Yuren, his father Wangu, and his mother née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Heng and Xuan, and his wife was née Xu. He placed thirtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zhenji, registered in an artisan household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Mengjing; he ranked sixth in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bozhou, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Wenjie, a County Magistrate; his father was Chi, and his mother née Yu. His parents and members of the grandparental generation were living. His elder brothers were Qianji, Zhanji, Shengji, and Fuji; his younger brothers were Mengji, Sunji, Fuji, and Yiji. His wife was née Chen. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ao Xian, registered in a civilian household in Gao'an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chunzhi; he ranked ninth in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Zhi, his father Long, and his mother née Zou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yue, an Investigating Censor, Rui, and Jing; his younger brothers were Quan, Jun, and Kai. His wife was née Fu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Pu 郭朴, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in a civilian household in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin; his grandfather, Qiang, was a county Registrar; his father was Qing, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shu, Zhen, and Dong, and his wife was née Li. He ranked fifty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Ying 任瀛, courtesy name Dengzhi, was registered in a military household of the Yanzhou Princely Guard in Shandong and was a native of Wenshui County, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Zi; his father, Zhen, held an honorary official title for longevity. His father's former wives were née Sun and née Bian; his mother was née Cai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuan, and his wife was née Hu. He ranked sixty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Hong 沈宏, courtesy name Weiyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ye; his grandfather was Chun; his father was Ding; his mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rong, and his wife was née Lu. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Wensheng 駱文盛, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in a civilian household in Wukang County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Shilong, was a Department Magistrate; his grandfather, Jia, was a Commissioner; his father was Run, and his mother was née Tang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Wenming, described as a clerk in Japan [?], Wenkui, and Wenzhen; his younger brother was Wenbing, and his wife was née Fei. He ranked twenty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yin Tai, courtesy name Chongji, was registered in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather, Xiang; his father, Shuang, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Kui, and his younger brother, Shu. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked seventieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kang Dahe, courtesy name Yuanzhong, was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a salt-producing household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun’an; his grandfather, Liangyi, held an honorary title conferred for longevity; his father was Changyuan; and his mother was née Cui. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Dachong. He married a woman née Cui. He ranked sixty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xueyan, courtesy name Youqian, was registered in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a civilian household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Lian, and grandfather, Yulin, both held honorary titles conferred for longevity. His father was Da’an; his mother was née Wei; and his stepmother was née Wu. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Xueshun, and his younger brother, Xuetong. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked sixteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Gu, courtesy name Zhongyi, was registered in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, in an artisan household, and was originally from Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather, Rong, held an honorary title conferred for longevity; his father was Sheng; his father’s former wife was née Wang; and his mother was née Qiang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tian. He married a woman née Chen. He ranked sixty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

高燿〔貫直隸保定府清苑縣民籍，增廣生，治詩經，字子潛，行一，年二十二，五月初六日生〕。曾祖安〔閘官〕，祖仲章，父顯宗〔監生〕，母李氏。重慶下，弟燦，娶黃氏。順天府鄉試第一百十六名，會試第七十名。

馬從謙〔貫應天府溧陽縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字益之，行四，年四十一，五月十二日生〕。曾祖信可，祖公輔〔封經歷〕，父忠，嫡母史氏，生母趙氏。慈侍下，兄從訓、從誨〔貢生〕、從謹〔義官〕、性魯〔知府，前兵科給事中〕，弟從言〔義官〕，娶丁氏，繼娶呂氏。順天府鄉試第一名，會試第二百四十六名。
translation_en:
Zheng Zhifu 鄭質夫, registered in an artisan household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zizhi; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-two years old, and was born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Qin, and his father Mingde; his mother was née Huang. His mother survived and his father was deceased. His younger brother was Hengfu, and his wife was née Lin. He placed forty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Xikui 趙希夔, registered in a commoner household in Changzhi County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yiqing; he ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xing, a military command official (bingma) [?]; his grandfather was Hui, a Catering Official; and his father was Bingzhong, a Department Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Du. His mother survived and his father was deceased. His elder brother Xiding was a Catering Official, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 311th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Yao 高燿, registered in a commoner household in Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added-quota government student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziqian; he ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-two years old, and was born on the sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was An, a Sluice Official; his grandfather was Zhongzhang; and his father was Xianzong, an Imperial University student. His mother was née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Can, and his wife was née Huang. He placed 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Congqian 馬從謙, registered in a commoner household in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yizhi; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was forty-one years old, and was born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xinke; his grandfather was Gongfu, honorifically invested as a Registrar; and his father was Zhong. His legal mother was née Shi, and his birth mother was née Zhao. His mother survived and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Congxun, Conghui (a tribute student), Congjin (an honorary official), and Xinglu [?] (a Prefect, formerly a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War); his younger brother Congyan was an honorary official. He married a woman née Ding and subsequently a woman née Lü. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
沈瀚〔貫直隸蘇州府吳江縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字原約，行一，年三十九，七月初二日生〕。曾祖政，祖達，父𤣱，前母王氏，母李氏。慈侍下，弟湛、淳、淶，娶顧氏。應天府鄉試第六十七名，會試第二百三十名。

艾希淳〔貫狹西延安府米脂縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字治伯，行二，年三十，十月十六日生〕。曾祖旺，祖文吉，父蕙〔典膳〕，母張氏，繼母高氏。慈侍下，兄希清、希仁、志仁，弟希淵、純仁，娶杜氏。狹西鄉試第三十四名，會試第一百二十五名。

沈應龍〔貫浙江湖州府烏程縣，民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字翔卿，行一，年三十，六月初一日生〕。曾祖士明，祖澄，父鑑〔知縣〕，前母胡氏，母朱氏。重慶下，弟應鵬、應鶚，娶花氏。浙江鄉試第八十二名，會試第三十二名。

錢衝〔貫江西臨江府新喻縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字貴徐，行五，年三十六，二月初七日生〕。曾祖忠顯，祖爵〔貢士〕，父瑞〔知縣〕，母翁氏。永感下，兄行、衎，弟術，娶謝氏。江西鄉試第十名，會試第一百八十九名。
translation_en:
Shen Han, registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanyue, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather Da, and his father 𤣱 [reading uncertain]; his father’s former wife was née Wang and his mother née Li; his father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Zhan, Chun, and Lai; his wife was née Gu; he placed sixty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ai Xichun, registered in Mizhi County, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhibo, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Wenji, and his father Hui, a Steward of Food; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Gao; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Xiqing, Xiren, and Zhiren, and his younger brothers Xiyuan and Chunren; his wife was née Du; he placed thirty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yinglong, registered in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Xiangqing, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shiming, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Jian, a District Magistrate; his father’s former wife was née Hu and his mother née Zhu; his parents and at least one grandparent were living; his younger brothers were Yingpeng and Ying’e; his wife was née Hua; he placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Chong, registered in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Guixu, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxian, his grandfather Jue, a tribute scholar, and his father Rui, a District Magistrate; his mother was née Weng; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Xing and Kan, and his younger brother Shu; his wife was née Xie; he placed tenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

方民悅〔貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣，軍籍，國子生，治《春秋》，字懋德，行一，年三十一，五月二十八日生〕。曾祖伯機，祖仕學，父鳳〔知縣〕，母陶氏。具慶下，弟民懌、民懷、民協、民恂，娶蔡氏。湖廣鄉試第十五名，會試第三百九名。

譙孟龍〔貫四川順慶府南充縣，民籍，國子生，治《易經》，字乾甫，行一，年三十三，四月二十一日生〕。曾祖明〔理問〕，祖崇儒〔典史〕，父暘〔知縣〕，母楊氏。具慶下，弟仲龍、季龍、吟龍、世龍、雲龍、見龍、攀龍、士龍、槐龍，娶柳氏。四川鄉試第四十名，會試第一百九名。

劉澍〔貫騰驤右衛籍，陝西西安府藍田縣人，國子生，治《易經》，字汝霖，行二，年四十一，九月二十八日生〕。曾祖得川，祖傑，父亨〔教諭，贈徵仕郎、吏科給事中〕，母宗氏〔贈孺人〕。永感下，兄瀹，弟濟〔刑科都給事中〕、汲、潠，娶白氏。順天府鄉試第九名，會試第二百六十八名。
translation_en:
Zhang Biao, registered in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Rushi; he ranked sixth in the family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the nineteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xiu, his grandfather Zhan, his father Dongyang, and his mother née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brothers are listed as Hang, Dong, Liangfu, Liangbi, Liangchen, Zhong, Yu, Mu, Ji, Duo, Guangshou, Jie, Cheng, Li, Guangzhou, Gui, Ge, and Geng [division of names uncertain]. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Minyue, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Maode; he ranked first in the family and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Boji, his grandfather Shixue, and his father Feng, a District Magistrate; his mother was née Tao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Minyi, Minhuai, Minxie, and Minxun. His wife was née Cai. He placed fifteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Menglong, registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Qianfu; he ranked first in the family and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ming, a Judicial Examiner; his grandfather was Chongru, a Clerk; and his father was Yang, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhonglong, Jilong, Yinlong, Shilong, Yunlong, Jianlong, Panlong, Shilong, and Huailong (the two names romanized Shilong are 世龍 and 士龍). His wife was née Liu 柳. He placed fortieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shu was registered with the Tengxiang Right Guard and was a native of Lantian County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Rulin; he ranked second in the family and was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Dechuan, his grandfather Jie, and his father Heng, an Instructor posthumously granted the titles Gentleman for Rendering Service and Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel. His mother, née Zong, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yue; his younger brothers were Ji 濟, Chief Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice, Ji 汲, and Xun. His wife was née Bai. He placed ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ouyang Huan, courtesy name Xuezhang, was registered in a civilian household in Wuqiang County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Zan, was a Sacrificial Attendant; his father was Lun, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shi, an Imperial University student, and Hui; his younger brothers were Yao, Xiao, and Xuan. His wife was née Guo. He ranked first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Dengying, courtesy name Yufu, was registered as a guardsman in the Ceremonial Guard Office of Lanzhou, Shaanxi, and was a native of Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture. A department school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was You; his grandfather, Jin; his father, Mao; and his mother, née Shao. His mother alone was living. His wife was née Du; he subsequently married a woman née Zheng. He ranked fifty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zongqi, courtesy name Shizhen, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Cheng, and grandfather, Xuan, both held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness. His father was Jiding, and his mother was née Chen. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Zongju and Zongyi. His wife was née Shu. He ranked eighty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Wenyou, courtesy name Shenfu, was registered in a military household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhang; his grandfather, Gao; his father, Ru, was an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Yang. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Wenzhi; his younger brothers were Wenzhong, Wengao, Wenkai, Wenshi, Wenti, and Wenmo. His wife was née Xie. He ranked eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Peng Dayou, courtesy name Ziqian, was registered in an officer household of Chenzhou Guard, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Qing and grandfather Luan were both Battalion Commanders; his father was Yan, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked forty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Jikui, courtesy name Ruiwen, was registered in a military household in Mengyin County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was eighth in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ping; his grandfather Zhong held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father was Jingren, and his mother was née Bao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhigao, Zhicheng, Zhihong, Zhiji (a student of the Directorate of Education), Zhiyong, Zhituan, and Zhishao; his younger brothers were Zhiqian, Zhijiu, Zhiwei, Zhixu, and Zhiwan. He married a woman née Bao. He ranked twentieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Chongqing, courtesy name Maozhen, was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Jiangyin County. An added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Shuduan, and his father Zheng; his mother was née Jiang, and his stepmother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Youqing and Yuqing. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Tang. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shu Ying, courtesy name Zhenbo, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was ninth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the nineteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Hao, and his father Rui; his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chun, and his younger brothers were Hong and Ying. He married a woman née Chai. He ranked fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fan Qing, courtesy name Yuanhui, was registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingzhi; his grandfather, Zhixin; his father, Chujin; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuanshu and Kang [?]; his younger brothers were Lin, Shu, Geng, Lang, and Xiang. He married a woman née Tu and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Fu, courtesy name Shaolin, was registered in a military household of the Yunnan Front Guard in Yunnan and was a native of Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Yan; his father, Luan; and his mother, née Shen. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Wentong and Wenda; his younger brothers were Qing, Xiang, Liangshi, Shangren, Shangyi, and Shangde. He married a woman née Ji. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Xuan, courtesy name Yuansu, was registered in a salt-producing household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked twenty-seventh in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the twentieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benshan; his grandfather, Gong; his father, Gao; and his mother, née Xu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Chun, Xu, Ying, Jin, Shou, Xun, Fang, and Ji; his younger brothers were Zu and Lian. He married a woman née Hu. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhen, courtesy name Maocheng, was registered in a military household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Huan, a prefectural assistant prefect posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Governance; his father was Shiguang, a Ceremonial Escort; and his mother was the Lady of Zaoyang County. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Lu, a Ceremonial Escort; Yin, an Usher; and Fei, Qin, Jin, Hua, E, Ai, and Ben. He married a woman née Tao and subsequently a woman née Ji. He placed forty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Chong, registered in an official household of the Front Battalion of the Baoding Rear Guard and a native of Renqiu County, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ziqian; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kan, a company commander; his grandfather was Ying; his father was Zhao; his mother was née Gao, and his stepmother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yi, Can, Xi, Ding (designated gangshi [?]), Jue, Zhang, Qi, Zi, Qin (a tribute scholar), and Qing (a student admitted by virtue of official family status); his younger brothers were Wei and Yue (a student admitted by virtue of official family status). He married a woman née Liu. He placed nineteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Min, registered in a military household of Shenzhou, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yuzhong; he ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather was Quan; his father was Siyi, an honorary official recognized for charitable service; and his mother was née Meng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Jue and Lu, and his younger brother was Pu. He married a woman née Yang. He placed ninety-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Lidao, registered in a military household of Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was an added student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Maozhong; he ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zihui, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Mian, posthumously granted the title of secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father was Biao, a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; and his mother was née Zhu, granted the title of Lady of Repose. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Chongdao, Wangdao, Tidao, Youdao, and Shundao. He married a woman née Tang. He placed thirty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yao, registered in a civilian household of Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Xiong; his father was Shangzhong; and his mother was née Shao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Wan, Guan, Yuan, Mian, Jian, Yun, Xu, Kui, and Xian. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ji Shichen, registered in a civilian household in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Siyong; he ranked fifth in family order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Lin was a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather Heng was a Prefectural Judge; and his father was Ang. His father’s former wife was née Yang, his stepmother née Gu, and his birth mother née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Liangchen, a student of the Directorate of Education, Kuichen, Longchen, Yaochen, Shunchen, and Zhongchen; his younger brother was Jinchen. His wife was née Shen. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yimo, registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shiwen; he ranked ninth in family order, was aged twenty-three, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Man, his grandfather Wenzheng, his father Shuyu, and his mother née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tong and Ji; his younger brothers were Xiang, Qi, Zi, Wu, and Zhen. His wife was née Chen. He placed seventeenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ru, registered in a civilian household in Fenzhou, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Pinqing; he ranked first in family order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Xing, his father Ziran, who held an honorary title for longevity, and his mother née Lei. His mother was living and his father deceased. His first wife was née Zhao, and his subsequent wife née Tian. He placed eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Tingchen, registered in a civilian household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shixian; he ranked third in family order, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhongli held an honorary title for philanthropy; his grandfather was Weiren, his father Wenpo, and his mother née Guan. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Tinghu, Tingjue, Tingdi, Tingyang, Tingkuang, Tingzhuo, who was designated for tribute-student status, Tingxian, a government-supported student, Ting’ai, and Tingwen. His wife was née Ju. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Chaoxiang 王朝相, registered in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhiyin; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, a Magistrate; his grandfather was Fan, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; his father was Ao, a subprefectural Clerk; and his mother was née Chang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chaoqing, and his younger brothers were Chaopin, Chaoju, Chaogong, and Chaobi. His wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhudong 劉注東, registered in Chiping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Siyu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather was Qing, and his father was Xian; his mother was née Zhu, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shundong, Midong, and Xingdong. His wife was née Shi. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ao Fan 敖璠, registered in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Guizhi; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renxian; his grandfather was Qi, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Yi; and his mother was née Lu. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Ke, Pei, and Huang. His wife was née Wu, and his subsequent wife was née Yu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tianlin 張天麟, registered in Shen Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a subprefectural school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yunzhen; he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather was Zuo, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; his father was Wenbi, a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Tianxiang, and his younger brothers were Tianqu, Tianchong, Tianxiu, Tianqi, and Tianjue. His wife was née Zu. He placed ninety-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lü Shao 呂韶, courtesy name Fengyi, was registered in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zigui; his grandfather, Dacai, received the title of Registrar by imperial bestowal; and his father, Chun, was a Department Vice Magistrate. His mother, née Shu, received the title of Lady (ruren) by imperial bestowal, and his stepmother was née Han. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Yin, was a County Assistant Magistrate; his younger brothers were Zhang, Xin, and Yun. He married a woman née Gao. He placed ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shida 李時達, courtesy name Zhongfu, was registered in Nanbu County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Xiang, was a County Assistant Magistrate; his grandfather was Tingxiang, and his father was Shilu. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Luo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Wenda, Minda, Congda, Yingda, Cida, Daoda, Huoda, and Chongda. He married a woman née Liu. He placed thirteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zeng 李增, courtesy name Mengchuan, was registered in Yingchuan Guard, Henan, in a military household. An attached student of the Yingzhou school in the directly administered region, specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Cong, and grandfather, Lan, each held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; his father, Bing, was an Imperial University student. His mother was née Liu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Kun, Cai, and Tan; his younger brothers were Jie, Yin, Shan, Jun, Yong, Ji, Tai, Jiong, Pei, Zai, and Kui. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed sixty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Yiguan 曹一貫, courtesy name Weifu, was registered in Shen County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Xing, was a Prefectural Registrar; his grandfather, Kai, held the honorary title of Longevity Official; and his father was Zhou. His mother was née Zhao. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Yikui. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Peng Feng 彭鳳 was registered in a civilian household in Fenyi County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Qizhi, and he ranked fourteenth among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-seven sui, born on the twelfth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Guan, a sacrificial attendant. His legal mother was née Huang, and his birth mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Jiao; his younger brothers were Huang, Luan, Hong, He, Yuan, Ti, Zhan, Shi, and Xiu. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Ruji 萬汝楫 was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan, and was a student of the department school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jiqing, and he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-one sui, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zongtian; his grandfather, Yonggao, held an honorary title for longevity; his father was Shui, and his mother was née Pang. His parents and grandparents were living. He married a woman née Xie. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Le 李樂 was registered in a military household in Luxi County, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Hezhong, and he ranked sixth among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-seven sui, born on the tenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Shiju; and his father, Tingpeng, a county magistrate. His mother was née Gong. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Tang, Xiang, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Gao, a sacrificial attendant; his younger brother was Ge. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Dong. He placed thirteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie You 謝佑 was registered in a civilian household in Songzi County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Defu, and he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins. He was twenty-nine sui, born on the fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather, Mao, was an examiner in a Provincial Administration Commission and was granted the title of investigating censor. His father, Shan, was an investigating censor; his mother, née Hu, was granted the title of Lady. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Zuo; his younger brothers were Pei, Jun, Yi, and Fen. He married a woman née Wu. He placed eighty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

郭鑒〔貫山西澤州高平縣，民籍，縣學生，治《春秋》，字允明，行五，年二十六，四月二十九日生。〕曾祖質〔知州〕，祖定〔知州〕，父坤〔知州〕，母王氏。慈侍下。兄鑾〔貢士〕、鍪〔行人〕、釡、鎜〔同科進士〕，弟鏨、鎣、鐆、鋈。娶申氏。山西鄉試第十六名，會試第二百五十九名。

孫植〔貫浙江嘉興府平湖縣，民籍，直隸華亭縣人，縣學生，治《書經》，字斯立，行四，年二十六，十月二十二日生。〕曾祖忠，祖軒〔封奉議大夫〕，父璽〔山西按察司僉事〕，母張氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下。兄棐、棟、杰。娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第四十八名，會試第六十八名。

張瀚〔貫浙江杭州府仁和縣，民籍，府學生，治《易經》，字子文，行六，年二十五，十一月三十日生。〕曾祖鵬〔義官〕，祖紀，父應祿，母李氏。具慶下。兄澣、潮、濓，弟濂〔貢士〕、浙、淳、洵、洽、浩、溉、澤、溹、洲、澋、洹、瀛、澐。娶陸氏。浙江鄉試第四十九名，會試第四十二名。

李載贄〔貫湖廣荊州府石首縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治《書經》，字進可，行四，年二十三，十一月初九日生。〕曾祖希鴻，祖椿〔教諭〕，父文炤，母黃氏。重慶下。兄載道、載事，弟載萬、載筆、載實。娶來氏。湖廣鄉試第十八名，會試第八十一名。
translation_en:
Guo Jian 郭鑒 was registered in a civilian household in Gaoping County, Zezhou, Shanxi, and was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yunming; he ranked fifth in his family and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhi, grandfather Ding, and father Kun were all department magistrates; his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Luan, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Mou, a Messenger; Fu; and Pan, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort. His younger brothers were Zan, Ying, Sui, and Wu. He married a woman née Shen. He placed sixteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Zhi 孫植 was registered in a civilian household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was originally from Huating County in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). He was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Sili; he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather Xuan received the honorary title Grand Master for Consultative Service; his father Xi was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in Shanxi; and his mother, née Zhang, received the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Fei, Dong, and Jie. He married a woman née Shen. He placed forty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Han 張瀚 was registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziwen; he ranked sixth in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Peng held honorary official status for public benefactions; his grandfather was Ji; his father was Yinglu; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Han 澣, Chao, and Lian 濓. His younger brothers were Lian 濂, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Zhe; Chun; Xun; Qia; Hao; Gai; Ze; Suo; Zhou; Hong 澋; Huan; Ying; and Yun. He married a woman née Lu. He placed forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zaizhi 李載贄 was registered in a civilian household in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jinke; he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-three years old, born on the ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xihong; his grandfather Chun was a county school Instructor; his father was Wenzhao; and his mother was née Huang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Zaidao and Zaishi; his younger brothers were Zaiwan, Zaibi, and Zaishi 載實. He married a woman née Lai. He placed eighteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
竇潤〔貫直隸滁州衛，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字子雨，行一，年四十四，七月十八日生〕。曾祖寄生，祖盛，父欽，母黃氏，繼母賈氏。具慶下，弟漢、淳，娶姜氏。應天府鄉試第一百三十四名，會試第一百七十九名。

鄭一統〔貫廣東潮州府揭陽縣，軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字朝慶，行一，年二十七，五月十四日生〕。曾祖克永，祖宜賑，父陽春，母劉氏。具慶下，弟一緒、一纘、一緝，娶陳氏。廣東鄉試第三十名，會試第八十八名。

陳元珂〔貫福建福州府閩清縣，民籍，懷安縣人，府學生，治春秋，字仲聲，行五，年三十一，十月初九日生〕。曾祖宗坦，祖聰，父良策，母吳氏。具慶下，弟元琰，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第四十二名，會試第一百三十二名。

陳椿〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣，民籍，吳江縣人，國子生，治易經，字子年，行二，年三十八，十月十四日生〕。曾祖珪〔壽官〕，祖銓，父澐〔醫學訓科〕，母顧氏。具慶下，兄貴〔監生〕，弟楫、桐、槐、枚、棉、楷、楠、集、李、枌、樾，娶陸氏。應天府鄉試第七十五名，會試第九十名。
translation_en:
Dou Run, registered in a military household of Chuzhou Guard in Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he was first in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the eighteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jisheng, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Qin; his mother was née Huang and his stepmother née Jia. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Han and Chun, and his wife was née Jiang. He ranked 134th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yitong, registered in a military household of Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chaoqing; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fourteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keyong, his grandfather Yizhen, and his father Yangchun; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yixu, Yizuan, and Yiji, and his wife was née Chen. He ranked thirtieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yuanke, registered in a civilian household of Minqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and a native of Huai’an County, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhongsheng; he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongtan, his grandfather Cong, and his father Liangce; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yuanyan, and his wife was née Zheng. He ranked forty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Chun, registered in a civilian household of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and a native of Wujiang County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zinian; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Quan, and his father Yun was an Instructor in the Medical School. His mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brother Gui was a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Ji, Tong, Huai, Mei, Mian, Kai, Nan, Ji, Li, Fen, and Yue. His wife was née Lu. He ranked seventy-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

江中躍〔貫四川重慶府巴縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字從之，行五，年二十一，六月二十六日生〕。曾祖熙暕，祖遂良〔封奉議大夫刑部郎中〕，父玠〔布政司左參政〕，嫡母李氏〔封宜人〕，生母黃氏。具慶下，兄中立〔知州〕、中能、中胤、中善、中孚、中才、中淵、中義、中曉，弟中輅，娶劉氏，繼娶白氏。四川鄉試第六十一名，會試第八十七名。
translation_en:
Xue Meng, courtesy name Weizheng, was registered in a civilian household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the fifteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Yu, an honorary official recognized for public service; his father was Yin, Director of Foodstuffs; and his mother was née Tao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xue, Director of Foodstuffs, Fu, and Shen; his younger brothers were Zi [?], Chun [?], an Imperial University student, Xiang, Hou, Li, Ju, and Jiao. He married a woman née Tang and subsequently a woman née Shen. He ranked thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Fuli, courtesy name Renfu, was registered in a civilian household in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. A government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Tan, posthumously appointed District Magistrate; his grandfather was Xian; his father was Huai; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Fushi and Fuchu. He married a woman née Zhao and subsequently a woman née Cui. He ranked thirty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Can, courtesy name Dehui, was registered in a salt-producing household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the twenty-second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shumei; his grandfather was Zhen; his father was Jing; and his mother was née Gu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yao, Chen, Zhang, Bi, Hu, and Lian. He married a woman née Yu. He ranked forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Zhongyue, courtesy name Congzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-one, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xijian; his grandfather was Suiliang, granted the titles of Grand Master for Counsel and Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; and his father was Jie, Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His legal mother was née Li, granted the title Lady of Suitability, and his birth mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhongli, a Department Magistrate, Zhongneng, Zhongyin, Zhongshan, Zhongfu, Zhongcai, Zhongyuan, Zhongyi, and Zhongxiao; his younger brother was Zhonglu. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Bai. He ranked sixty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

方孟縉〔貫江西南昌府武寧縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字文卿，行九，年四十一，八月十四日生〕。曾祖景華，祖汝寧，父璞，母吳氏。永感下，兄孟經、孟緯，弟孟紳，娶黃氏。江西鄉試第一百六十三名，會試第一百八十名。
translation_en:
Yuan Xichang, registered in Meizhou, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boxiang, his grandfather Dadan, and his father Qi, an honorary official for longevity; his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gunchang and his younger brother Xiuchang. He married a woman née Ma and subsequently a woman née Cheng. He placed sixty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Kuan, registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Lifu; he ranked eleventh in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lizhang, his grandfather Sanxi, and his father Zhenyan; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Chengqi. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed fifty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Xian, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zicheng; he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Jing, and his father Shan; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Qiao. He placed twenty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Mengjin, registered in Wuning County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Wenqing; he ranked ninth in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinghua, his grandfather Runing, and his father Pu; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mengjing and Mengwei, and his younger brother was Mengshen. He married a woman née Huang. He placed 163rd in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

沈夢鯉〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字龍卿，行一，年三十六，九月二十八日生〕。曾祖浤，祖輔，父芳，母余氏，繼母壽氏。重慶下，弟夢麟、夢熊、夢黿、夢鯨、夢鹿、夢鵰、夢鰲、夢相、夢豸，娶孫氏。浙江鄉試第六十六名，會試第二十名。

陳天然〔貫廣東瓊州府瓊山縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝中，行五，年三十，十一月二十六日生〕。曾祖才望，祖徵，父瑞〔壽官〕，母孫氏，生母吳氏。具慶下，兄天祺、天祐、天祐，弟天熈，娶王氏。廣東鄉試第五十二名，會試第一百十八名。

劉佐〔貫山東濟南府德州，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字才甫，行一，年二十二，四月二十九日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖玉，父福，母張氏。重慶下，弟俚、儒、份，娶賀氏。山東鄉試第七十一名，會試第五十二名。
translation_en:
Shen Mengli, courtesy name Longqing, was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Fu, and his father Fang; his mother was née Yu and his stepmother née Shou. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Menglin, Mengxiong, Mengyuan, Mengjing, Menglu, Mengdiao, Meng’ao, Mengxiang, and Mengzhi; his wife was née Sun. He placed sixty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Liangbi, courtesy name Mengxian, was registered in an artisan household of the Wugong Central Guard and was a native of Qiantang County, Zhejiang; he was an added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Fu, and his father Yue; both his grandfather and father held honorary official status for longevity. His father’s former wife was née Zhang, his legal mother née Hou, and his birth mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Liangxiang; he married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Pang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Tianran, courtesy name Ruzhong, was registered in Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Caiwang, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Rui, who held honorary official status for longevity; his mother was née Sun and his birth mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tianqi, Tianyou, and Tianyou [name repeated in the transcription; ?], and his younger brother was Tianxi; his wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zuo, courtesy name Caifu, was registered in Dezhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Yu, and his father Fu; his mother was née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Li, Ru, and Bin (份); his wife was née He. He placed seventy-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

蕭體元〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣人，河南南陽府新野縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字善復，行二，年三十八，十一月二十二日生〕。曾祖孔資〔教諭〕，祖聰〔教諭〕，父麟〔知縣〕，母朱氏，繼母李氏。具慶下，弟慶元，娶曹氏。河南鄉試第八十名，會試第二百四十一名。
translation_en:
Shi Qianxiang, courtesy name Shanzheng, was registered in a salt-producing household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the tenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Gong, his grandfather Ying, his father Renjun, and his mother née Fang; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qianfu and Qianlu, and his younger brothers Qianyou and Qianzu. He married a woman née Xue. He ranked seventy-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Shizhao, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in a commoner household in Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Ding and grandfather Hou both held honorary longevity titles; his father was Zhongliang, with the annotation “Yu” [?]. His mother was née Huang and his stepmother née Mo; his father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brother was Shishu. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Hai. He ranked eleventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Tianzi, courtesy name Ruxue, was registered in a salt-boiling household in Raoping County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A county-school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yongfu, his grandfather Huangong, his father Jingshen, and his mother née Fan; his mother was deceased, and he attended his surviving father. His younger brothers were Tiande, Tiankai, and Tianyi. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Huang. He ranked fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Tiyuan, courtesy name Shanfu, was a native of Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a commoner household in Xinye County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Kongzi and grandfather Cong were both Instructors; his father Lin was a District Magistrate. His mother was née Zhu and his stepmother née Li; both parents were living. His younger brother was Qingyuan. He married a woman née Cao. He ranked eightieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Chun, registered in Kaihua County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dewan. Fifth in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Qian; and his father, Hong, a Prefectural School Instructor. His mother was née Wu. His mother alone was surviving. His elder brothers were Cheng, Qing, and Tang; his younger brothers were Zi and Huang. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pu Ze, registered in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Renbo. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanqing; his grandfather, Shou; and his father, Long. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother was née Cao. His father alone was surviving. His elder brothers were Hai and Yuan. He married a woman née Liu. He placed eleventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yun, registered in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to an artisan household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shuqing. Third in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather, Ming; and his father, Chen. His mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhen and Zhan. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Ao, registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shihua. Eighth in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhong, was granted the titles of Gentleman for Rendering Virtue (Chengde lang) and Assistant Prefect. His grandfather, Hao, was a Prefect, promoted to the prestige title Yazhong dafu. His father, Jia, was a County School Instructor, granted the titles of Grand Master for Upright Service (Fengzhi dafu) and Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, with the additional privilege of wearing fourth-rank official dress. His mother, née Du, was granted the title Lady of Suitability (Yiren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ao [?—the same name as the candidate in this transcription], a Grand Master for Constitutional Service (Zhongxian dafu) and Prefect; Yi, holder of a seventh-rank titular office; Jing, Vice Prefect of Yanzhou and formerly Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Guan, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. He married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Dong, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was an attached student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuelong. He ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather, Huai, was a County Clerk; his father, Jue, was a Ceremonial Usher; and his mother was née Su. His grandparents and parents were living. He married a woman née Lü. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Sirong, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shengzhi. He ranked second among his brothers and was forty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qi, received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather, Yan, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his father was Feng, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sien. He married a woman née Xia and subsequently a woman née Lu. He placed twenty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kang Lang, registered in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yonghui. He ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan; his grandfather was Bai; his father was Jiong. His father’s former wife and his mother were both née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shuo and Hu. He married a woman née Xie and subsequently women née Xie and née Lian. He placed twelfth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Rulin, registered in Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student at the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhongwang. He ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-four, born on the sixteenth day of the intercalary fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qing, was posthumously granted the title Gentleman for Rendering Virtue; his grandfather, Lan, was a Principal Adjudicator; and his father, Bingzhong, was a Professor. His father’s former wife was née Gu, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruxian, Ruyi (a metropolitan graduate of the preceding examination), Rubi, and Ruwei; his younger brothers were Ruji and Rumei. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Nie. He placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.
