translation_en:
Zhu Xie 諸燮, courtesy name Zixiang, was registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Ding; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yi, and his wife was née Li. He placed fifty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Chengxue 馬承學, courtesy name Hongdao, was registered in a medical household attached to the Imperial Medical Office and was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the Southern Metropolitan Region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather Rong was officially honored as a righteous commoner and granted the cap and girdle of rank. His father Ji was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother Chengye was also a student of the Directorate of Education. His wife was née Wang 汪. He placed 121st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Fan 吳藩, courtesy name Jiafu, was registered in a civilian household in Quanjiao County, Chuzhou, in the Southern Metropolitan Region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather Xian was a school instructor, and his father Ji was an assistant instructor. His mother was née Yue. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Zao, and his wife was née Yang. He placed eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Jiujing 吳九經, courtesy name Zicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. An annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dang, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Hai; his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jiuchou, Jiufeng, and Jiuxiao, and his wife was née Wang 王. He placed fifty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Fu, from Tong’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yaoxi; he was fifth in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shijia; his grandfather, Chunyang, held an honorary longevity title; and his father was Liangxuan. His father’s former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Jue, Zhi, Gong, and Yu. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Tianzuo, from Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was registered in a civilian household and was an attached student of the prefectural Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zibi [?]; he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiyan, his grandfather was Zhongping, and his father was Lang; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tianzheng, Tianfu, Tianshen, and Tianjue. He was betrothed to a woman née Wu. He placed fifty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Jun, from Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Pingshu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qian, was a district magistrate; his grandfather, Xuan, held an honorary longevity title; and his father was Tang. His mother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Song, and his younger brothers were Qin and Yu. He married a woman née Shen. He placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Weifan, from Liaozhou, Shanxi, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural Confucian school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zijie; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, his grandfather was Shun, and his father was Ying. His mother was née Fan, and his stepmother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Weiyuan, Weiping, Weihan, and Weicheng. He married a woman née Pei and subsequently a woman née Han. He placed fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third class: 227 men, granted the status of equivalent metropolitan graduate (jinshi).

Feng Tianyu, registered in a civilian household in Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yingfang; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Ao, was a government school student; his father, Peng, was an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Tianjun, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Gai, registered in a civilian household in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shijie; he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Fuying, received successive posthumous honors as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Works, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. His grandfather, Min, received the honorary appointment of Professor and successive posthumous honors as Specially Advanced Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Left Pillar of State, Junior Guardian concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. His father, Ji, held the titles of Specially Advanced Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Left Pillar of State, Junior Guardian concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Scrupulous Conduct. His mother, née Gong, received successive honors culminating in Lady of the First Rank. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother, Fen, was Prefectural Judge of Shuntian; his younger brothers were Qing, a tribute scholar; Qu, a Director in the Ministry of Rites; and Ye and Ji, students admitted by virtue of official family status. His wife was née Bi; he subsequently married women née Cai and née Hou. He placed ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Fu was registered in a military household of the Wuxiang Left Guard and was a native of Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mengfu; he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Jian, his father Ming, and his mother née Jin. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Zan, and his wife was née Feng. He placed eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Lian, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Weijian; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Jun was posthumously appointed Assistant Prefect; his grandfather Lan was Vice Prefect. His father was Da, his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Qian. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Wen, Jing, Gun, Shu, Fu, Xu, Yi, and Ying. He married a woman née Shao. He placed thirtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Tingji, registered in a scholarly household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Liren; he ranked tenth among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Guan was posthumously appointed District Magistrate and, through successive posthumous promotions, Minister of Personnel at Nanjing. His grandfather Yuanmei was Prefect and received successive posthumous promotions to Minister of Personnel at Nanjing. His father Han was Minister of War at Nanjing, posthumously appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Wen’an. His legal mother, née Huang, was granted the title Lady for Compliance and subsequently received the posthumous title Lady of the First Rank; his birth mother was née Zhu. He placed eleventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Chongxin, registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhonglü; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-two years old, born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Buce [?], his grandfather was Shanjing, his father was Rumin, and his mother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Chongluo [?] and Chongyan. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventy-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shangyi, registered in a military household in Fenzhou, Shanxi, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bozheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhu; his grandfather Zhi was District Magistrate; his father Shifang was District Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Shangli. He married a woman née Song. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Cheng, a District Magistrate posthumously granted the rank of Gentleman of the Civil Service (Wenlin lang); his grandfather was Xijie, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner promoted in honorary rank to Grand Master of the Lesser Center (Yazhong dafu); his father was Mi, an Imperial University student; his mother and stepmother were both née Zhang; his parents and at least one grandparent were living; his elder brothers were Zhong, Zhen, Nan [?], and Guan, and his younger brother was Xun; his wife was née Xu; he placed fourteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Sicheng, his grandfather was Gong, his father was Zheng, and his mother was née Han; his mother alone survived; his elder brothers were Da and Chaofu, and his younger brothers were Tong and Shi; his wife was née Zhao; he placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lai Pin 來聘, registered in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Anguo, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the sixth day of the fifth lunar month. He Yan, registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was Instructor at the county school of Hui'an, Fujian. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shanchong, and he ranked first in his family. He was forty-two years old, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shiliang, his grandfather Lian, and his father Qianzhi; his mother was née Mai. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ming, Cuo, Yong, Quan, and Zhen. His wife was née Huang. He placed thirteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shu Ting, registered in a civilian household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Shao'an, and he ranked first in his family. He was thirty-eight years old, born on the first day of the intercalary eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Demao, his grandfather Tan, and his father Qin; his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Huai and Jiang, and his younger brothers Yang and He. His wife was née Li. He placed eighty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shouyue was registered with Pengcheng Guard and was a native of Changsha County, Huguang. He was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunzhong, and he ranked third in his family. He was twenty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Fusheng was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. His grandfather Chun was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Constitutional Service and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, and subsequently the additional titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. His father Zhixue was Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Justice. His father's former wife, née Wang, and his mother, née Chen, were both posthumously granted the title Lady (shuren). His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Shouyu and Shouqian, the latter a Vice Director in the Ministry of War. His younger brothers were Shoumo, Shoulu (a tribute scholar), Shourang, Shoupu, Shouchu, and Shoujie. His first wife was née Pan; he subsequently married a woman née Ru. He placed ninety-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Zhizhen, registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Congjing, and he ranked fourth in his family. He was nineteen years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Qiong (a County Vice Magistrate), and his father Zhao; his mother was née Yao. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Cheng'en, Chengxian, and Zhicai. His younger brothers were Zhiqing, Zhisi, Zhile, Zhidao, Zhiwu, Zhiqi, Zhimeng, Zhizhong, Zhiqi, Zhitai, Zhixiao, and Zhiwen. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

高時〔貫浙江杭州府臨安縣民籍，歲貢生，治易經，字中行，行十八，年三十，正月初一日生〕。曾祖澄浩〔義官〕，祖良毓〔義官〕，父文華，母童氏。具慶下，兄圻、陞，弟坰、垿、陛、陵、罔、墅、陸，娶胡氏。順天府鄉試第七十名，會試第一百七十六名。

陳紹〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字用光，行八，年三十五，十一月二十日生〕。曾祖滂，祖頊，父述，母嚴氏。具慶下，兄緒，弟維、絳、綰，娶鍾氏。浙江鄉試第五十一名，會試第一百九十名。

趙大佑〔貫浙江台州府太平縣軍籍，縣學生，治春秋，字世胤，行一，年二十六，六月十一日生〕。曾祖堅，祖崇賢〔知州〕，父相，母王氏。重慶下，弟大佃、大佶，娶牟氏。浙江鄉試第七十二名，會試第十六名。

蔡其潮〔貫浙江嘉興府海鹽縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字時信，行四十四，年四十五，正月二十六日生〕。曾祖富〔壽官〕，祖全，父珙，母徐氏。慈侍下，兄澣、津、瀾、滇、相、松、滔、淳、演、瀅，弟〔其禮、其章、其甫、其門、其進、其海、其淮、其濤、其淶、其沾、其澳〕，娶姚氏。浙江鄉試第五十四名，會試第一百五十名。
translation_en:
Gao Shi, of civilian registration in Lin’an County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongxing; he ranked eighteenth in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Chenghao, and grandfather, Liangyu, both held honorary office for public benefactions; his father was Wenhua and his mother was née Tong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi and Sheng; his younger brothers were Jiong, Xu, Bi, Ling, Wang, Shu, and Lu. He married a woman née Hu. He placed seventieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shao, of civilian registration in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yongguang; he ranked eighth in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pang, his grandfather Xu, his father Shu, and his mother née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xu; his younger brothers were Wei, Jiang, and Wan. He married a woman née Zhong. He placed fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Dayou, of military registration in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shiyin; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-six years old, born on the eleventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Chongxian, was a Department Magistrate; his father was Xiang and his mother née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Dadian and Daji. He married a woman née Mou. He placed seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Qichao, of civilian registration in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shixin; he ranked forty-fourth in birth order and was forty-five years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Fu, held honorary office conferred for longevity; his grandfather was Quan, his father Gong, and his mother née Xu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Huan, Jin, Lan, Dian, Xiang, Song, Tao, Chun, Yan, and Ying; his younger brothers were Qili, Qizhang, Qifu, Qimen, Qijin, Qihai, Qihuai, Qitao, Qilai, Qizhan, and Qi’ao. He married a woman née Yao. He placed fifty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Yingxiang, registered in an officer household of Changsha Guard, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bozheng; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Yong, grandfather Gang, and father, whose name is transcribed as 𤣱 [?], were all Company Commanders; his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingqi, Yingheng, Yingshao, Yingkui, and Yingchang. He married a woman née Hu. He placed sixty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Mengxiang, registered in a military household of Jianli County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an attached government-school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Youzheng; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the ninth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather Yanjing held the honorary title of Official of Righteousness; his father was Kun, and his mother was née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Mengxi. He married a woman née Lü. He placed twenty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Yingyang, registered in a civilian household of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Junmin; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Ying was an Instructor; his grandfather was Yu, his father was Shen, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingsu, Yingdun, Yingqian, Yinggao, Yingkui (應夔), Yingqi, and Yingkui (應奎). He married a woman née Pan, subsequently married a woman née Sun, and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Wang. He placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Tingyong, registered in a civilian household of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruxing; he ranked third in birth order, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Shu, his grandfather was Ganlin, his father was Deqing, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tingxuan, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, Tingyi, and Tingli; his younger brothers were Tingliang, Tingben, Tingxiu, Tingchen, and Tingji. He married a woman née Song. He placed thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiao Lian, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture, in a civilian household. A student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked first in family birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Sen, was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Tang; his mother was née Ma, and his stepmothers were née Shang and née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rui and Huan, and his younger brothers were Gong, Can, Dai, and Min. He married a woman née Liang and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xi Liangfu, courtesy name Shiqing, was registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Lun, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Qin; his mother and stepmother were both née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Liangbi and Liangyi. He married a woman née Tang. He placed forty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ji, courtesy name Wenxi, was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked forty-fifth in family birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shujin; his grandfather was Gang; his father was Yi; and his mother was née Sun. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Zong. He married a woman née Weng. He placed sixty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shanglin, courtesy name Zijian, was registered in Shanyang County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Ang; his grandfather was Yu; his father, Rong, held an honorary official title for longevity; his mother was née Fan, and his stepmothers were née Wang and née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Luan, and his younger brothers were Ao, Jing, Shangdong, Ke, and Zhi. He married a woman née Dai. He placed eighty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

温學舜〔貫福建泉州府晋江縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字憲統，行一，年三十三，九月初三日生〕。曾祖良〔中書舍人〕，祖玉〔訓導〕，父夔，母蔡氏。具慶下。弟學周、學閔。娶李氏。福建鄉試第四十名，會試第二百七十六名。

羅椿枝〔貫浙江嚴州府桐廬縣，匠籍，國子生，治書經，字日新，行二，年三十二，四月初五日生〕。曾祖永明，祖儒〔訓導〕，父翔鳳，母陳氏，繼母朱氏。具慶下。兄桂枝，弟楠枝、橡枝、松枝。娶張氏，繼聘姚氏。浙江鄉試第七十八名，會試第三百四名。
translation_en:
Wang Zun, courtesy name Zifa, was registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bing, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Shang; his father was Xide, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Ren. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, Qian, Da, Yao, Gao, and Ting, an Investigating Censor; his younger brothers were Zhui, Yu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Lin, Qian, and Shu. His wife was née Han. He placed thirty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji, courtesy name Weiyi, was registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. An additional student of the local government school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jixian; his grandfather was Shen, a District Magistrate; and his father was Dan. His legal mother was née Wan, his stepmother née Zhou, and his birth mother née Wan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gui and Ji, and his younger brothers Fei and An. His wife was née Ye. He placed seventy-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Xueshun, courtesy name Xiantong, was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, a Secretariat Drafter; his grandfather was Yu, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Kui; and his mother was née Cai. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xuezhou and Xuemin. His wife was née Li. He placed fortieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Chunzhi, courtesy name Rixin, was registered in Tonglu County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an artisan household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongming; his grandfather was Ru, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Xiangfeng; his mother was née Chen; and his stepmother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Guizhi, and his younger brothers were Nanzhi, Xiangzhi, and Songzhi. He married a woman née Zhang and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Yao. He placed seventy-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 304th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王崇冠〔貫山西太原府榆次縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字雅夫，行二，年二十八，十一月二十五日生〕。曾祖軏，祖景春，父明，前母原氏，母賈氏。慈侍下，兄崇仁，娶郝氏，繼娶張氏。山西鄉試第六名，會試第二百一名。

薛應旂〔貫直隸常州府武進縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字仲常，行二，年三十六，十一月初四日生〕。曾祖瑞，祖锳，父卿，母史氏，繼母吳氏。具慶下，兄應廷，弟應辰、邦臣、應嘉，娶馮氏。應天府鄉試第九十名，會試第二名。

周尚忠〔貫直隸河間府景州吳橋縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯顯，行二，年三十五，二月二十五日生〕。曾祖政，祖裕〔陰陽官〕，父冕〔壽官〕，嫡母牟氏，生母李氏。具慶下，兄尚志〔貢士〕，弟尚勤、尚友、尚恩，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第五十二名，會試第二十七名。

顧承芳〔貫直隸鳳陽府臨淮縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字子譽，行一，年三十九，六月十七日生〕。曾祖震〔順天府治中，贈通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，祖佐〔資善大夫、戶部尚書，贈太子太保〕，父伯謙〔貢士〕，母康氏。永感下，弟承恩、承德、承勛、承忠、承志、承顏、承順、承緒、承顯，娶蔡氏，繼娶潘氏。應天府鄉試第四名，會試第二百八十七名。
translation_en:
Wang Chongguan, registered in Yuci County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yafu; he ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-eight sui, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yue, his grandfather Jingchun, and his father Ming; his father's former wife was née Yuan, and his mother was née Jia. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Chongren. He married a woman née Hao and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Yingqi, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongchang; he ranked second among his brothers, was thirty-six sui, and was born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rui, his grandfather Ying, and his father Qing; his mother was née Shi and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingting, and his younger brothers were Yingchen, Bangchen, and Yingjia. He married a woman née Feng. He placed ninetieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Shangzhong, registered in Wuqiao County, Jing Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Boxian; he ranked second among his brothers, was thirty-five sui, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather Yu was an official of a School of Yin and Yang; and his father Mian held an honorary rank granted for longevity. His legal mother was née Mou and his birth mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother Shangzhi was a tribute student; his younger brothers were Shangqin, Shangyou, and Shang'en. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Chengfang, registered in Linhuai County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-nine sui, and was born on the seventeenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhen was an Assistant Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Zuo was Grand Master for the Fostering of Goodness and Minister of Revenue, posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. His father Boqian was a tribute student, and his mother was née Kang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Cheng'en, Chengde, Chengxun, Chengzhong, Chengzhi, Chengyan, Chengshun, Chengxu, and Chengxian. He married a woman née Cai and subsequently a woman née Pan. He placed fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

馬九德〔貫直隸德州衛軍籍，山東青州府益都縣人，州學生，治詩經，字子懋，行二，年二十四，正月初七日生〕。曾祖雄，祖昌，父亨衢〔知縣〕，母焦氏。具慶下，兄九皐，弟九鼎、九疇、九遷、九萬、九功、九淵，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第十二名，會試第十名。

楊時秀〔貫直隸鳳陽府懷遠縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字叔茂，行三，年三十八，四月初十日生〕。曾祖銑，祖成，父窴〔教諭〕，母張氏。具慶下，兄堂、奎，娶徐氏。應天府鄉試第十名，會試第六十一名。
translation_en:
Lu Lin, registered in an artisan household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiufu; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deqing, his grandfather Minzheng, and his father Dounan; his father's former wife was née Huang, and his mother was née Shu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wang, and his younger brothers were Shi and Li. His wife was née Zhu. He placed thirtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Long, registered in a civilian household in Lin'an County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruhua; he ranked tenth in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ren, his grandfather Guan, his father Cheng, and his mother née Jiang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Luan, Feng, Peng, and Jing. His wife was née He. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Jiude, registered in a military household of Dezhou Guard in Zhili and originally from Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the subprefectural school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zimao; he ranked second in his family and was twenty-four years old, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiong, his grandfather Chang, and his father Hengqu, a county magistrate; his mother was née Jiao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiugao, and his younger brothers were Jiuding, Jiuchou, Jiuqian, Jiuwan, Jiugong, and Jiuyuan. His wife was née Wang. He placed twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shixiu, registered in a civilian household in Huaiyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the county school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shumao; he ranked third in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Tian, an instructor; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tang and Kui. His wife was née Xu. He placed tenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖十四年進士登科錄

張舜臣〔貫山東濟南府章丘縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字熈伯，行二，年三十，十月二十七日生〕。曾祖恂，祖紞〔壽官〕，父燦〔義官〕，前母王氏，母劉氏。具慶下，兄堯臣〔省祭官〕，娶魏氏。山東鄉試第二名，會試第二百五十一名。

吳鏌〔貫福建福州府長樂縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字利用，行五，年三十七，八月二十四日生〕。曾祖彬，祖炳〔壽官〕，父璽，母高氏，繼母高氏。具慶下，兄釗、鈴、鏘，弟鑄、鉞、鎰、鏗、錦、鑑、鐸，娶鄭氏，繼娶黃氏。福建鄉試第五十四名，會試第二百三十三名。

戴夢桂〔貫山東濟南府濟陽縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字仲芳，行二，年三十九，十二月十七日生〕。曾祖景忠，祖禎，父禮〔知縣〕，嫡母李氏，生母張氏。慈侍下，兄夢賢〔主簿〕，娶郭氏，繼娶劉氏。山東鄉試第八名，會試第四十二名。

劉大直〔貫四川寧川衛軍籍，成都府華陽縣人，國子生，治詩經，字養浩，行二，年三十四，九月二十四日生〕。曾祖晟，祖志宏，父佐〔壽官〕，母袁氏。具慶下，兄大正，弟大宜、大立、大全，娶王氏。四川鄉試第二十三名，會試第一百三十三名。
translation_en:
Zhang Shunchen, courtesy name Xibo, was registered in a military household in Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather, Dan, held an honorary longevity title; and his father, Can, held an honorary title for charitable service. His father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Yaochen, was a Sacrificial Attendant. His wife was née Wei. He placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Mo, courtesy name Liyong, was registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather, Bing, held an honorary longevity title; and his father was Xi. His mother and stepmother were both née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhao, Ling, and Qiang; his younger brothers were Zhu, Yue, Yi, Keng, Jin, Jian, and Duo. His wife was née Zheng, and his subsequent wife was née Huang. He placed fifty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Menggui, courtesy name Zhongfang, was registered in a military household in Jiyang County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jingzhong; his grandfather was Zhen; and his father, Li, was a District Magistrate. His legal mother was née Li, and his birth mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother, Mengxian, was a Registrar. His wife was née Guo, and his subsequent wife was née Liu. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Dazhi, courtesy name Yanghao, was registered in a military household of Ningchuan Guard, Sichuan, and was a native of Huayang County, Chengdu Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Zhihong; and his father, Zuo, held an honorary longevity title. His mother was née Yuan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dazheng; his younger brothers were Dayi, Dali, and Daquan. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

郭盤〔貫山西澤州高平縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字允新，行四，年三十三，十二月初三日生〕。曾祖質〔知州〕，祖定〔知州〕，父城〔州判〕，母李氏。嚴侍下，兄鑾、塏、鋆〔行人〕、釜，弟鑒〔同科進士〕、鍳、鎣、鎏、錅，娶趙氏。山西鄉試第六十四名，會試第二百四十二名。

胡崇德〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，竈籍，國子生，治書經，字伯賢，行二十三，年三十二，十一月初五日生〕。曾祖宜孫，祖紹，父丙，母童氏。慈侍下，兄崇元、崇仁、崇政、崇儉、崇禮，弟崇學、崇智，娶岑氏。浙江鄉試第九十名，會試第三百十二名。

翁五倫〔貫浙江紹興府蕭山縣，民籍，附學生，治書經，字大經，行一，年二十九，七月十八日生〕。曾祖秉，祖文〔訓導〕，父堯，母蕭氏。重慶下，弟五常、五章、五言、五音，娶徐氏，繼娶張氏。浙江鄉試第七十名，會試第一百五十二名。

黎堯勳〔貫四川潼川州樂至縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子欽，行一，年三十三，九月十六日生〕。曾祖希賢〔壽官〕，祖禎〔壽官〕，父邦屏，母趙氏。重慶下，弟堯華、堯鄰，娶張氏。四川鄉試第十五名，會試第二百五十六名。
translation_en:
Guo Pan 郭盤 was registered in Gaoping County, Zezhou, Shanxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Yunxin and ranked fourth among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhi and grandfather Ding were Department Magistrates; his father Cheng was an Assistant Department Magistrate, and his mother was née Li. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Luan 鑾, Kai 塏, Yun 鋆, a Messenger, and Fu 釜; his younger brothers were Jian 鑒, a jinshi of the same examination cohort, Jian 鍳, Ying 鎣, Liu 鎏, and Li 錅. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Chongde 胡崇德 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a salt-producing household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Boxian and ranked twenty-third among his brothers. He was thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yisun, his grandfather Shao, his father Bing, and his mother née Tong. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Chongyuan, Chongren, Chongzheng, Chongjian, and Chongli; his younger brothers were Chongxue and Chongzhi. He married a woman née Cen. He placed ninetieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Wulun 翁五倫 was registered in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An attached student of the local government school specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Dajing and ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bing; his grandfather Wen was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Yao, and his mother was née Xiao. His parents and at least one grandparent were still living. His younger brothers were Wuchang, Wuzhang, Wuyan, and Wuyin. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yaoxun 黎堯勳 was registered in Lezhi County, Tongchuan Department, Sichuan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Ziqin and ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xixian and grandfather Zhen both held honorary official status conferred for longevity; his father was Bangping, and his mother was née Zhao. His parents and at least one grandparent were still living. His younger brothers were Yaohua and Yaolin. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

閔煦〔貫直隸河間府任丘縣籍，松江府上海縣人，縣學生，治詩經，字和卿，行三，年二十九，十月初十日生〕。曾祖琦〔贈山西左布政使〕，祖定〔贈山西左布政使〕，父槐〔按察司副使〕，母顏氏〔封恭人〕。具慶下，兄勳〔義官〕、燾〔監生〕、然、杰〔監生〕，弟照、熈。娶李氏。順天府鄉試第四十八名，會試第二百三十五名。
translation_en:
Gao Dui 高對, courtesy name Zhonglong, was registered in a military household of the Dali Guard in Yunnan and was a native of Wenchuan County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather, Xin, held an honorary office for longevity; his father, Ang, was a county magistrate; and his mother was née Zhou. His father was living. His elder brothers were Peng and Song, and his younger brothers were Qi, Zheng, Cen, Dong, and E. He married a woman née Xiong and subsequently a woman née Qian. He placed sixteenth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Kuang 余爌, courtesy name Deming, was registered in a civilian household in Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouzeng; his grandfather, Rongfu; his father, Zhi; and his mother, née Peng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiong, Kui, Hui, and Chi. He married a woman née Xia. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Feng 陳鳳, courtesy name Yubo, was registered in an official household of the Nanjing Rear Guard of the Rear Military Commission and was a native of Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Lin; and his father, Gang. His father's former wife was née Huang, his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Wei. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Min Xu 閔煦, courtesy name Heqing, was registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qi, and grandfather, Ding, were each posthumously awarded the title of Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi. His father, Huai, was a vice commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission, and his mother, née Yan, was granted the title Lady of Respect. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun, an honorary official for charitable contributions; Tao, an Imperial University student; Ran; and Jie, an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Zhao and Xi. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Pixian, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and served as Instructor in the county school of Xiuning, in the directly administered region (Zhili). He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xianwen; he ranked sixth in birth order and was forty-two years old, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zeren, his grandfather Mengshen, and his father Dexuan; his mother was née Lin and his stepmother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Pizheng, and his younger brothers were Wenshu, Wenke, Picheng, and Wenzhi. He married a woman née Zheng, and subsequently women née Chen and née Lin. He placed seventy-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Pei, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Chaoming; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanding, his grandfather Dexiang, and his father Qi; his mother was née Yao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xi and Hui. He married a woman née Li. He placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Yi, registered in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Wanqing; he ranked tenth in birth order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuo, his grandfather Qi, and his father Chuan; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Hu. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Liangcai, registered in Taizhou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili), belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Ru, an Assistant Instructor, and his father Cong; his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Liangchen and Liangshi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Weiyue, courtesy name Yaochen, was registered in a military household of the Hangzhou Right Guard in Zhejiang. An annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was forty-one years old, born on the third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Hao, and father, Qi, had each been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations. His mother was née Mi, and his stepmother née Fu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ting and Weifan, and his younger brothers Weihan and Weizhong. His wife was née Cao. He placed forty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yingkui, courtesy name Ruwen, was registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was originally from Xiuning County in Zhili. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fuyuan, his grandfather Guicheng, his father Zhenfu, and his mother née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yingqi, Yinghui, Yingxiang, Yingyou, and Yingsu. His wife was née Ying. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Maoshang, courtesy name Gongfu, was registered in a civilian household in Mianzhou, Sichuan. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in birth order and was forty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Zhongben, his father Chu, a student of the Imperial University, and his mother née Guo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Maoguan, and his younger brothers Maohe, Maojing, Maozhao, Maoxun, and Maojian. His wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Yuling, courtesy name Daoyan, was registered in a military household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the eighth day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather Gao held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father Tingchen was a Ceremonial Escort, the husband of an imperial clanswoman. His mother was the Lady of Xinping County, and his stepmother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Zhou. He placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳東光〔貫河南開封府鈞州匠籍，州學生，治書經，字叔晦，行一，年二十九，五月三十日生〕。曾祖綱，祖謙，父璣，母馬氏。具慶下，弟東輝、東漸，娶劉氏。河南鄉試第六十五名，會試第一百四十五名。

顧霑〔貫浙江嘉興府海鹽縣竈籍，府學生，治詩經，字少雨，行一，年三十一，二月二十一日生〕。曾祖廷用，祖仁，父愷，母莊氏。重慶下，弟霽，娶管氏。浙江鄉試第十八名，會試第二百七十八名。
translation_en:
Zhu Wenzhi, courtesy name Binfu, was registered in a military household in the Rear Battalion of Yunnan Front Guard and was originally from Haiyan County, Zhejiang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ang; his grandfather was Jun, an honorary official for longevity; and his father was Xi. His father’s former wife was née Mao, and his mother was née Wang. His parents and a grandparent or grandparents were living. His younger brother was Wenxian, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed first in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Tong, courtesy name Boyi, was registered in a military household in Lintong County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Mengsi; his grandfather was Jing, an Assistant Prefect; and his father was Zongwen, an honorary official for longevity. His mother was née Chen, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ning, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan), Shou, Ding, Nai, and Ang; his younger brothers were Jing and Bian. His wife was née Niu. He placed fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dongguang, courtesy name Shuhui, was registered in an artisan household in Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirtieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather was Qian, and his father was Ji. His mother was née Ma, and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Donghui and Dongjian, and his wife was née Liu. He placed sixty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Zhan, courtesy name Shaoyu, was registered in a salt-producing household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Tingyong, his grandfather was Ren, and his father was Kai. His mother was née Zhuang. His parents and a grandparent or grandparents were living. His younger brother was Ji, and his wife was née Guan. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Xiu, courtesy name Shifu, was registered in Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household and was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-three by traditional reckoning, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianwen, his grandfather Tianling, and his father Can; his father's former wife was née Xia and his mother née Peng, and both parents were living. His elder brother was Wei and his younger brother Ji; he married a woman née Fang. He placed seventy-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yaonian, courtesy name Shaozhong, was registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household and was an expanded-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; he ranked seventh among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight by traditional reckoning, and was born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ke, his grandfather Fu, his father Lan, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living, and he married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tong Hanchen, courtesy name Zhongliang, was registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an artisan household and was an expanded-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight by traditional reckoning, and was born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Fu, his father Wei, and his mother née Shen; both parents were living, his elder brother was Shunchen, and he married a woman née Liu. He placed eleventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yun, courtesy name Shixin, was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household and was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-one by traditional reckoning, and was born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie, an Instructor, his grandfather Rugui, his father Jingwei, and his mother née Li; both parents were living, his younger brother was Fei, and he married a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Yingqi 林應麒, registered in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Biren; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daben, his grandfather Wenkui, his father Jian, and his mother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Yingpeng, and his wife was née Ying. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Jimeng 趙繼孟, registered in Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongzhi; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-one, and was born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Hou, his father Chong, and his mother née Meng. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jijue, Jizu, Jizong, and Jixian. He married a woman née Yan and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Li. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Bing 孫昺, registered in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shanghui; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Ying, his father Lu, his mother née Cao, and his stepmother née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother or stepmother was living. His elder brother was Ang, and his wife was née Li. He placed twenty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yunkui 何允魁, registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Kesheng; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Rong held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather Zhang was a Left Administrator; his father Li held an honorary official title for public beneficence; and his mother was née Kuang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jizhi, a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and Shaoke; his younger brothers were Shaoxian, Zuzhi, Wanzhi, and Yunzhao. His wife was née Zhou. He placed sixty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

蕭祥曜〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字文奎，行三，年二十七，七月初八日生〕。曾祖季脩〔贈給事中〕，祖彥德，父甫璽，母陳氏。永感下，兄祥曦、祥暘，娶王氏。江西鄉試第二名，會試第二百六十六名。

吳從義〔貫福建福州府福清縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治春秋，字思忠，行二，年三十九，二月初七日生〕。曾祖穆，祖公讓，父朝佐，母林氏。永感下，兄從周，弟從心、從嘉、從明，娶俞氏。福建鄉試第七十三名，會試第二百五十五名。

向宗哲〔貫四川成都府資縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字汝賢，行一，年三十九，十一月三十日生〕。曾祖敬〔知府〕，祖璽〔同知〕，父艾，母蔡氏。具慶下，弟宗啓、宗喬、宗善、宗呂、宗師、宗亨，娶熊氏。四川鄉試第八名，會試第二百六十四名。
translation_en:
Chen Hu, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruqi. He ranked fifth among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong; his grandfather, Kuan; his father, Min, held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Conduct; and his mother was née Sheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were En, a student of the Directorate of Education, Shan, Xian, and Zhi; his younger brothers were Hui, Fang, Pin, Yu, and Zhang. His wife was née Shen. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Xiangyao, registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wenkui. He ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jixiu, posthumously appointed Supervising Secretary; his grandfather, Yande; his father, Fuxi; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xiangxi and Xiangyang. His wife was née Wang. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Congyi, registered in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Sizhong. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mu; his grandfather, Gongrang; his father, Chaozuo; and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Congzhou; his younger brothers were Congxin, Congjia, and Congming. His wife was née Yu. He placed seventy-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Zongzhe, registered in Zi County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruxian. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, a Prefect; his grandfather, Xi, a Vice Prefect; his father, Ai; and his mother was née Cai. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zongqi, Zongqiao, Zongshan, Zonglü, Zongshi, and Zongheng. His wife was née Xiong. He placed eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陸坤〔貫陝西蘭州儀衛司校籍，直隸崑山縣人，州學生，治易經，字子厚，行一，年二十九，六月二十七日生〕。曾祖海，祖岳，父爻〔監生〕，母楊氏。重慶下，弟基、奎、坦、塋，娶孫氏。陝西鄉試第二十九名，會試第二百八十一名。

translation_en:
Zhang Hu 張祜, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was registered in an officer household of Yongchang Guard, Yunnan, and was a native of Nanyang Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yu, Deputy Battalion Commander; his grandfather was Kang; his father was Hua, an honorary official for longevity; and his mother was née Du. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Zhe and Mao, and his wife was née Ruan. He placed forty-fifth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Hu 楊祜, courtesy name Shoufu, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yong, a tribute student; his grandfather was Hao, a provincial sacrificial official; his father was Tingzhen; and his mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qi and Zuo, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 316th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Kun 陸坤, courtesy name Zihou, was registered in a guardsman's household of the Ceremonial Guard Office in Lanzhou, Shaanxi, and was a native of Kunshan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather was Yue; his father was Yao, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Yang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ji, Kui, Tan, and Ying, and his wife was née Sun. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Daochong 任道充, courtesy name Shaoxu, was registered in a military household in Xiaoyi County, Fenzhou, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Wengan; his father was Shu, a District Magistrate; his father's former wife was née Yan; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Daoyuan, and his wife was née Wu. He placed nineteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Feng Liangzhi, registered in an official household of Lin’an Guard, Yunnan, was a native of Huangpi County, Huguang, and a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yangwu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Min; his father was Ji; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Liangneng, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed forty-sixth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ai Pu, registered in a commoner household of Yongfeng County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziwen; he ranked tenth among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuwang; his grandfather was Duanhe; and his father was Rui, an Assistant Instructor. His father’s former wife was née Zou, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Xiao. He placed eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ye, registered in a military household of Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yunmeng; he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather was Hong, an honorary official for longevity; his father was Cai; and his mother was née Xue. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Bing, Can, and Chuo; his younger brothers were Yao, Xi, and Lian. His wife was née Ouyang. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Renlong, registered in a military household of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Ziqian; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Nian; his grandfather was Xixian, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Zheng, granted the privilege of wearing official cap and belt under provisions of imperial grace; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Renjie, Renru, Renyang, and Yuchun; his younger brothers were Renyan, Renfeng, Renlun, Renchen, Renyi, Renlin, Rentong, Rensi, Renbiao, Renjia, Renxiong, and Renqi. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eighty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

治詩經字子一行一年二十三正月十三日生
曾祖剛 祖仕英 父勤 母屈氏

四川鄉試第十一名 會試第四十一名
punctuated:
鄭錫麒〔貫福建福州府長樂縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字獻禎，行六，年二十三，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖肅，祖世傑，父勉，母劉氏。具慶下，弟錫熊、錫騵、錫鯨、錫驄，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第八十三名，會試第二百四十九名。

錢泮〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字鳴教，行一，年四十二，正月二十日生〕。曾祖建〔義官〕，祖諤〔義官〕，父鯆，母褚氏。具慶下，兄秩、冠、宦、伸、察、寵，弟激、和、燥、倣、作、洽、煉、剃，娶徐氏，繼娶盧氏。應天府鄉試第六十名，會試第一百八十七名。

高節〔貫陝西西安後衛官籍，山東禹城縣人，國子生，治詩經，字仲立，行一，年三十八，十一月二十日生〕。曾祖玉〔百戶〕，祖鐸〔百戶〕，父昇〔百戶〕，母吳氏〔封安人〕，繼母唐氏。重慶下，弟第、策，娶陳氏。陝西鄉試第二名，會試第二十八名。

牟朝宗〔貫四川叙州府宜賓縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字子一，行一，年二十三，正月十三日生〕。曾祖剛，祖仕英，父勤，母屈氏。慈侍下，娶李氏。四川鄉試第十一名，會試第四十一名。
translation_en:
Zheng Xiqi, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xianzhen, he ranked sixth in family order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Su, his grandfather Shijie, his father Mian, and his mother née Liu; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xixiong, Xiyuan, Xijing, and Xicong, and his wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Pan, registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mingjiao, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged forty-two, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Jian and grandfather E both held the honorary designation of Righteous Official; his father was Pu and his mother née Chu, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi, Guan, Huan, Shen, Cha, and Chong; his younger brothers were Ji, He, Zao, Fang, Zuo, Qia, Lian, and Ti [?]. His wife was née Xu, and he subsequently married a woman née Lu. He placed sixtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Jie was registered in an officer household of the Xi'an Rear Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Yucheng County, Shandong. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongli, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Yu, grandfather Duo, and father Sheng each served as Battalion Commander; his mother, née Wu, was granted the title Lady of Peace, and his stepmother was née Tang. Grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Di and Ce, and his wife was née Chen. He placed second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mou Chaozong, registered in a civilian household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziyi, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Shiying, his father Qin, and his mother née Qu; his father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Li. He placed eleventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

邵基〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣竈籍，國子生，治書經，字子厚，行一，年三十四，十月初二日生〕。曾祖有容，祖蒙〔七品散官〕，父煉〔按察司副使〕，母陳氏，繼母金氏。重慶下，弟𡌨，娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第三十五名，會試第四十七名。

王嘉元〔貫四川叙州府宜賓縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字仁仲，行一，年二十八，正月二十二日生〕。曾祖永麘〔驛丞〕，祖應嵩〔教諭〕，父璧，母羅氏，繼母王氏、劉氏。重慶下，弟嘉輅，娶曹氏。四川鄉試第五十六名，會試第一百四十二名。

李槩〔貫廣東肇慶府四會縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字時勵，行四，年三十一，十一月初五日生〕。曾祖府〔壽官〕，祖鏆〔義官〕，父永福〔七品散官〕，母羅氏。重慶下，兄梁、棐、新，弟檠、槊、桼，娶陳氏。廣東鄉試第六十名，會試第二百五名。

聶靜〔貫江西吉安府永豐縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字子安，行十二，年二十九，六月二十二日生〕。曾祖日聰，祖玉治〔封文林郎〕，父洪，母張氏。具慶下，弟靛，娶王氏。江西鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百七名。
translation_en:
Shao Ji, registered in a salt-producing household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zihou, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yourong; his grandfather, Meng, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his father, Lian, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; his mother was née Chen, and his stepmother née Jin. His parents and grandparents were living; his younger brother was Pi 𡌨 [?], and his wife was née Shen. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiayuan, registered in a civilian household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Renzhong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather, Yongxiang, was a Station Master; his grandfather, Yingsong, was a School Instructor; his father was Bi; his mother was née Luo, and his stepmothers were née Wang and née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living; his younger brother was Jialu, and his wife was née Cao. He placed fifty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Gai, registered in a civilian household in Sihui County, Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shili, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Fu, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather, Guan, held an honorary official title for public benefactions; his father, Yongfu, held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his mother was née Luo. His parents and grandparents were living; his elder brothers were Liang, Fei, and Xin, his younger brothers were Qing, Shuo, and Qi, and his wife was née Chen. He placed sixtieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and two hundred fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Nie Jing, registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zi'an, he ranked twelfth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Ricong; his grandfather, Yuzhi, had been conferred the title Gentleman of Scholarly Excellence; his father was Hong, and his mother was née Zhang. Both his parents were living; his younger brother was Dian, and his wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.
