王世雍〔貫山東兖州府東平州汶上縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字堯治，行一，年三十五，正月二十三日生〕。曾祖釗，祖端〔封知縣，進監察御史服色，贈太僕寺少卿〕，父杲〔大理寺左少卿〕，母郭氏〔累贈恭人〕，繼母許氏〔封孺人，贈恭人〕、李氏。具慶下，弟世熈、世泰，娶郭氏。山東鄉試第三十五名，會試第一百五十一名。

劉鳳池〔貫陝西西安府渭南縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字文甫，行一，年三十二，三月二十二日生〕。曾祖孝徵，祖才〔巡檢〕，父潮，母冉氏。慈侍下，弟鳳山，娶任氏。順天府鄉試第八名，會試第三十六名。

吳瓊〔貫直隸徽州府祁門縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字德輝，行三十一，年三十八，七月初十日生〕。曾祖敬宗，祖信〔知縣〕，父文教，母許氏。永感下，娶許氏。應天府鄉試第五十六名，會試第五十四名。

趙炳然〔貫四川保寧府劔州，民籍，國子生，治書經，字子晦，行二，年二十九，十一月十八日生〕。曾祖佐〔知縣〕，祖思濟，父松，母鄭氏。重慶下，兄挺然，娶王氏。四川鄉試第六十一名，會試第一百十名。
translation_en:
Wang Shiyong, courtesy name Yaozhi, was registered in a civilian household in Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong; a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao; his grandfather Duan was honorarily appointed Magistrate, granted the dress and insignia of an Investigating Censor, and posthumously appointed Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his father Gao was Left Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; his mother, née Guo, received successive posthumous honors as Lady of Respect (gongren); and his stepmothers were née Xu, appointed Lady of Goodness (ruren) and posthumously honored as Lady of Respect, and née Li. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Shixi and Shitai, and his wife was née Guo. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Fengchi, courtesy name Wenfu, was registered in a military household in Weinan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiaozheng; his grandfather Cai was a Chief of Police; his father was Chao, and his mother was née Ran. His mother was living and his father deceased; his younger brother was Fengshan, and his wife was née Ren. He placed eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Qiong, courtesy name Dehui, was registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked thirty-first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the tenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingzong; his grandfather Xin was a Magistrate; his father was Wenjiao, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were deceased, and his wife was née Xu. He placed fifty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Bingran, courtesy name Zihui, was registered in a civilian household in Jian Subprefecture, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Zuo was a Magistrate; his grandfather was Siji; his father was Song, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living; his elder brother was Tingran, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

王喬齡〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字維岳，行四十二，年三十八，十月初一日生〕。曾祖謨，祖淵，父椿，母熊氏。具慶下，弟高、嵩，娶夏氏，繼娶趙氏。浙江鄉試第二十四名，會試第七十六名。

汪宗凱〔貫湖廣武昌府崇陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字子才，行二，年二十八，四月二十九日生〕。曾祖璉〔壽官〕，祖藻〔監生，封兵部主事〕，父文明〔知縣〕，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄宗元〔行人司行人〕，弟宗皐、宗伊〔貢士〕、宗召、宗夔、宗南、宗光、宗介、宗茂、宗說、宗恭，娶陳氏。湖廣鄉試第三十四名，會試第六十二名。

包孝〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣，民籍，浙江嘉興縣人，縣學增廣生，治禮記，字元愛，行十二，年二十八，二月二十五日生〕。曾祖俊〔封南京禮部郎中〕，祖鼎〔知府，進階亞中大夫〕，父志〔監生〕，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄洪、浩、泳、淳、濂、漢、節〔前科進士〕、深、潔，弟汴、治、澤，娶曹氏。應天府鄉試第六十一名，會試第一百三十八名。
translation_en:
Xu Guanzhi, courtesy name Daoqing, was registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty-one, born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng, his grandfather Peng, his father Jing, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Shen. He placed thirty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qiaoling, courtesy name Weiyue, was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked forty-second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-eight, born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mo, his grandfather Yuan, his father Chun, and his mother née Xiong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Gao and Song. He married a woman née Xia and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zongkai, courtesy name Zicai, was registered in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Zao, an Imperial University student granted the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of War; his father was Wenming, a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Zongyuan, a Messenger in the Messenger Office. His younger brothers were Zonggao, Zongyi (a tribute scholar), Zongzhao, Zongkui, Zongnan, Zongguang, Zongjie, Zongmao, Zongshuo, and Zonggong. He married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Xiao, courtesy name Yuan'ai, was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, in a civilian household, and was originally from Jiaxing County, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked twelfth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, granted the honorary title of Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Ding, a Prefect promoted to the rank of Grand Master of Lesser Centrality (yazhong dafu); his father was Zhi, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Hong, Hao, Yong, Chun, Lian, Han, Jie (a metropolitan graduate of the preceding examination), Shen, and Jie; his younger brothers were Bian, Zhi, and Ze. He married a woman née Cao. He placed sixty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

曹韓〔貫陝西西安府咸寧縣，軍籍，府學生，治易經，字可宗，行一，年三十一，正月初七日生〕。曾祖福〔贈行太僕寺卿〕，祖恭〔贈行太僕寺卿〕，父蘭〔左布政使〕，母王氏〔封淑人〕。具慶下，弟䎐、朝、輖、軼、軒、趼。娶管氏，繼娶吉氏。陝西鄉試第三十九名，會試第二百二十四名。

鄭寅〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字思敬，行四，年四十五，十月初十日生〕。曾祖仕讓，祖叔倫，父文榮，母夏氏，繼母趙氏。慈侍下，弟憲、寬、蒙、密、宗。娶錢氏，繼娶鄒氏。浙江鄉試第十六名，會試第二百七十三名。

王維楨〔貫陝西西安府華州，民籍，州學生，治詩經，字允寧，行三，年二十九，十一月初二日生〕。曾祖和，祖源，父載，母劉氏。慈侍下，兄維藩、維祺，弟維新、維厚。娶東氏。陝西鄉試第五十一名，會試第九十六名。
translation_en:
Zhang Fu 張輻, courtesy name Wenheng, was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked twenty-fourth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chou; his grandfather, Cai, was a Police Chief; his father was Lu; and his mother was née Shi. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Zhen, and his younger brothers were Yuan, Lu, Zi, Zhou, and Zhou. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Han 曹韓, courtesy name Kezong, was registered in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather, Fu, and grandfather, Gong, were both posthumously granted the title Chief Minister of the Branch Court of the Imperial Stud. His father, Lan, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Virtue. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chao 䎐, Chao 朝, Zhou, Yi, Xuan, and Jian. He married a woman née Guan and subsequently a woman née Ji. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yin 鄭寅, courtesy name Sijing, was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty-five, born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shirang; his grandfather, Shulun; his father, Wenrong; his mother, née Xia; and his stepmother, née Zhao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Xian, Kuan, Meng, Mi, and Zong. He married a woman née Qian and subsequently a woman née Zou. He placed sixteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Weizhen 王維楨, courtesy name Yunning, was registered in Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-nine, born on the second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was He; his grandfather, Yuan; his father, Zai; and his mother, née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Weifan and Weiqi, and his younger brothers were Weixin and Weihou. He married a woman née Dong. He placed fifty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Xu 張緒, registered in a civilian household in Xiajiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Qingli; he ranked tenth in birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Fu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner responsible for military preparedness; his grandfather was Gui; his father was Fenyong; and his mother was née Ruan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Ji, Hui, and Tong. He married a woman née Yuan and subsequently a woman née Xiao. He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhichen 王之臣, registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingchong; he ranked third in birth order and was forty-seven years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zuo; his grandfather was Shouyue, an Instructor granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Yiyan, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; and his mother was née Li, granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhongchen and Xinchen, and his younger brothers were Xiangchen, Yaochen, and Dingchen. He married a woman née Yin. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tang 王鏜, registered in a military household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an supplementary student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Mengsheng; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather was Kuang, a provincial graduate (juren) serving as Acting Assistant Instructor; his father was Jie, a Prefectural Vice Prefect; and his mother was née Weng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jian, Ying, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, Qi, and Jun. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed sixty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Dou 牛斗, registered in a civilian household in Shanyang County, Huai'an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yunzhang; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jun, a Postal Station Master; his grandfather was Xiong; his father was Fan, a retired Department Magistrate advanced to the prestige rank of Grand Master of Court Ranks (chaolie dafu); and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother Shan was a Departmental Clerk. He married a woman née Lu. He placed twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Fang, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Laifu; he ranked eleventh in family order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wende, his grandfather Gang, and his father Guan; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiang and Yong, and his younger brothers Li, Zhi, Liang, and Gao. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zan Rusi, registered in a civilian household in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zixue; he ranked sixth in family order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xingzong, his grandfather Gong (a clerk, with the designation transcribed as 豐吏 [?]), and his father Fuxing; his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruheng, Ruyi, Rusheng, Ruxin, and Rushuang. He married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yuan, registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and originally from Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, was an additional-quota student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyong; he ranked first in family order and was thirty-four years old, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zonghai, his grandfather Zhiyu, and his father Jingzhi; his father’s former wife was née Shen and his mother née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Huaishan, and his younger brothers Shi, Quan, Yao, Yue, and Zhen. He married a woman née Bu. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Tengjiao, registered in a military household in Weinan County, Huazhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an additional-quota government-school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shihua; he ranked second in family order and was twenty-five years old, born on the second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Di, his grandfather Wenying, and his father Long (holder of an honorary longevity title); his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother Tengxiao was a Station Master. He was betrothed to a woman née Zhao. He placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qian Bangyan 錢邦彦 was registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zhizheng and was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather Yi and father Yinglong were both Chief Geomancers in schools of yin and yang. His mother was née Teng, and his stepmothers were née Ge and née Ji. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Bangzhi. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Yang. He ranked forty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Dan 汪旦 was registered in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household, and was a native of Jinjiang County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zhaozhong and was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Yangqing was an annual tribute student; his grandfather Zhineng held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his father Han was a District Magistrate. His mother was née Chen. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Shu and his younger brother Xin. He married a woman née Wu. He ranked fortieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Mengbi 王夢弼 was registered in Dai Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Weixiao and was first in birth order, aged thirty, born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather Jun was a Prefectural Vice Prefect; his grandfather Xu held an honorary official title awarded for charitable contributions; and his father Shizhong was a Subprefect. His mother was née Dong. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Mengxiong, Mengrao, and Mengsong; his younger brothers were Meng[?] 夢𥡠, Mengqi, Mengxiang, Mengsui, and Mengpi. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Qixian 黃齊賢 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Rusi and was fifteenth in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Lian, his grandfather Jing, and his father Shi; his mother was née Ye. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Jingxian and Lixian. He married a woman née Lu. He ranked seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

江應選〔貫浙江衢州府常山縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字尚實，行三十，年三十五，九月二十四日生〕。曾祖文華，祖克賔，父鋌〔教諭〕，母汪氏。具慶下，兄應舉、祜、詢、觀瀾、尚占、良才〔貢士〕，娶何氏。浙江鄉試第六十七名，會試第一百二十二名。

劉汀〔貫直隸真定府冀州南宮縣，民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字叔南，行二，年二十六，五月十五日生〕。曾祖明，祖幹〔壽官〕，父錫〔知縣，封監察御史〕，母張氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄濂〔監察御史〕，弟濤、藻、沱、渚，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第一百八名，會試第一百九十六名。
translation_en:
Yang Jiang 楊獎, registered in a salt-producing household in Anyi County, Jiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Maode, he ranked third in family birth order, and he was thirty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao, his grandfather Jing 靖, and his father Jing 景, an honorary official for public beneficence; his father's principal wife was née Sun, and his birth mother was née Song. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Lu and Chang, his younger brothers Fan and Huan, and his wife was née Cao. He placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ge Jin 葛縉, registered in a civilian household in Changyi County, Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhongrong, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was twenty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junyong, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Qing, a Police Chief; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Jing, a tribute student, Wei, and Ji, his younger brothers Lun and Chun, and his wife was née Fu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Yingxuan 江應選, registered in a civilian household in Changshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shangshi, he ranked thirtieth in family birth order, and he was thirty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenhua, his grandfather Kebin, and his father Ting, an Instructor; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Yingju, Hu, Xun, Guanlan, Shangzhan, and Liangcai, the last a tribute student, and his wife was née He. He placed sixty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ting 劉汀, registered in a civilian household in Nangong County, Jizhou, Zhending Prefecture, the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shunan, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was twenty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Gan, an honorary official recognized for longevity, and his father Xi, a District Magistrate granted the honorary title of Investigating Censor; his mother, née Zhang, was granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living; his elder brother Lian was an Investigating Censor, his younger brothers were Tao, Zao, Tuo, and Zhu, and his wife was née Li. He placed 108th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

周鳳岐〔貫福建建寧府浦城縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字文徵，行二，年二十一，十月初二日生〕。曾祖理安，祖洪，父瑚〔監生〕，母陳氏。具慶下，兄鳳鳴〔監生〕，弟鳳儀、鳳韶。聘真氏。福建鄉試第二十三名，會試第二十八名。
translation_en:
Li Yu, registered in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Weizhong; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu; his grandfather, Feng, had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and belt under the applicable regulations. His father, Yingkui, was an Admonisher. His mother was née Dong, and his stepmothers were née Mu and née Lü. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother Nian was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year; his younger brothers were Ci, Ren, Que, Yi, Gan, Ken, Xian, Ping, and Zong. He married a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Rao Xiang, registered in Dapu County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhiyin; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather was Shiduan; his father was Jingji; and his mother was née Fan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Dong, Mo, Kai, and Dang. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently married another woman née Huang. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Guangyu, registered in Linjin County, Pu Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Boqian; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather was Jin; his father was Qianyi; and his mother was née Li. Both his parents were living. His elder brother was Guangshi, and his younger brothers were Guangzhou, Guangzhai, and Guangting. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently married a woman née Wei. He placed tenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Fengqi, registered in Pucheng County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenzheng; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-one years old, born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li'an; his grandfather was Hong; his father, Hu, was a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Chen. Both his parents were living. His elder brother Fengming was also a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Fengyi and Fengshao. He was betrothed to a woman née Zhen. He placed twenty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fang Jie, registered in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zihe; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongming; his grandfather, Yu, held an honorary official title for charitable contributions; and his father, Jian, was an annual tribute student. His mother was née Wu, and his stepmother née Qi. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Nian, Ren, and He. He married a woman née Tang and subsequently a woman née Hu. He placed eighty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Wancheng, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhituan; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the thirtieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chaogong, his grandfather Hengsi, and his father Guozhen. His mother was née Chen, and his stepmother née Weng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wanli, Wanshan, and Wantiao. He married a woman née Lin. He placed twentieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Minyue, registered in the Taiyuan Front Guard, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weigong; he ranked first in birth order, was aged forty-four, and was born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Qing, and his father Zheng, who held an honorary official title for charitable contributions. His mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Lei. He placed twentieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zichen, registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a physician household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weiren; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, a tribute student; his grandfather was Yan, and his father Zheng. His mother was née Luo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ji, a Judicial Examiner; Ze, a tribute student; Juan, a Department Magistrate in Sichuan; and Mengchen. His younger brothers were Shunjian, Shunsheng, Zhongchen, Liangchen, Hanchen, Wangchen, Fuchen, and Jinchen. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Sanjie, registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a native of Kunshan County and a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rukang, and he ranked third in family order. He was twenty-nine, born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun (holder of an honorary title for longevity); his grandfather was Hui (Gentleman for Rendering Service); his father was Shiyang (an Imperial University student awaiting selection for office); and his mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Renyong (tribute student) and Sanxi (jinshi and subprefectural magistrate); his younger brothers were Sangu, Sanpin, and Sanchong. His wife was née Gui. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Dayong, registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Daoxing, and he ranked second in family order. He was thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lai; his grandfather was Rongfu; and his father was Weichai (holder of an honorary title for longevity). His father's former wife was née Liu, and his mother was née Huang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Qiang, and his wife was née Lin. He placed fifty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 313th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lianggui, registered in a military household in Wen'an County, Bazhou Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyuan, and he ranked first in family order. He was thirty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Wei; his father was Jue (Registrar); and his mother was née Sun. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Lianghan and Liangxiang; his younger brothers were Liangjue, Liangzhong, Liangneng, Liangchou, Liangcai, and Liangdong. His wife was née Meng. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Kai, registered in an artisan household in Jiangshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dahe, and he ranked 116th in family order. He was thirty, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youde (holder of an honorary title for longevity); his grandfather was Shi'an; his father was Benrong; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zili, Ziyi, and Zicai; his younger brothers were Zizhi, Ziti, Zigong, and Ziyi. His wife was née Yang. He placed twentieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Qin 李秦 was registered in a civilian household in Linzhang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zhongxi and ranked third among his brothers. He was twenty-nine, born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun; his grandfather, Jian; and his father, Fu, held the honorary title of Longevity Official. His father’s former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhen and Tai; his younger brothers were Chunzhong and Fengchun (name division uncertain [?]). He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Chun 宿椿 was registered in a banner household of the Shenyang Commandery Herds Office in Shanxi and was a native of Yuci County. A student of the Lu’an Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Kongling and ranked ninth among his brothers. He was thirty-two, born on the fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qing, was an official awaiting selection for appointment; his grandfather, Zhao, was an Imperial University student; and his father, Zheng, was a Consort. His father’s former wife was née Han, the Lady of Laiwu County; his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tang and Gen, both Honorary Officials; Yuan; Song; Dong, a Director of Food Services; Yi; Xiang; and Yu. His younger brothers were Kai, Ying, Pu, Wu, Zhen, and Shan, all government school students; Kui; Feng, an Honorary Official; Fen; and Bi. He married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Yingmin 蘇應旻 was registered in a military household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Youqing and ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Eju; his grandfather, Ziyi; and his father, Zheng, was an Assistant Instructor. His legal mother was née He, and his birth mother was née Xu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Yingkui and Yingxing. He married a woman née Han. He placed eleventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xian 陳暹 was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Dehui and ranked ninth among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhou, had been granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather, Shufu, had been posthumously granted the same title. His father, Wei, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, advanced to the rank of Grand Master of Court Array. His legal mother, née Ye, had been granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Lin. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Ju, a tribute scholar; Chi, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Pei; Da, Grand Coordinator of Shanxi and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief; Tai; and Jin, an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Lin. He placed ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

姚悳〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字維順，行九十七，年四十，四月十二日生〕。曾祖悌〔贈都察院右副都御史〕，祖坰〔署訓導事，舉人〕，父鏌，前母王氏，母王氏。永感下，兄泮、泙、淶〔左春坊左諭德〕，弟沐、汲〔中軍都督府都事〕，娶劉氏，繼娶馬氏。浙江鄉試第四十九名，會試第一百三十九名。

李念〔貫山西太原府平定州軍籍，國子生，治書經，字惟克，行一，年二十九，九月初六日生〕。曾祖璞，祖鳳〔遇例冠帶〕，父應奎〔紀善〕，母董氏，繼母穆氏、呂氏。重慶下，弟愈〔同科進士〕、慈、憨、稔、意、感、懇、憲、憑、總，娶王氏。山西鄉試第二十名，會試第一百九十三名。

俞則全〔貫浙江紹興府新昌縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字祖修，行十一，年二十六，十月二十一日生〕。曾祖叔光〔壽官〕，祖振英〔奉政大夫，尚寶司卿〕，父朝衮〔七品散官〕，母王氏。具慶下，兄則廉，弟則徵、則家，娶呂氏。浙江鄉試第七十八名，會試第十四名。
translation_en:
Shu Qian 舒遷 was registered in a civilian household in Yi County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yuqiao and ranked fifth in his family. He was thirty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jingchun; his grandfather, Changsheng; and his father, Sizhong. His father's former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yi, and his younger brother was Jin. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed 125th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao De 姚悳 was registered in a military household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Weishun and ranked ninety-seventh in his family. He was forty, born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather, Ti, was posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Jiong, was a provincial graduate who served as acting Assistant Instructor. His father was Mo; his father's former wife and his mother were both née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Pan, Peng, and Lai, the last serving as Left Mentor of the Left Spring Office. His younger brothers were Mu and Ji, the latter serving as a Chief Clerk in the Chief Military Commission of the Center. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Ma. He placed forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Nian 李念 was registered in a military household in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Weike and ranked first in his family. He was twenty-nine, born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Pu; his grandfather, Feng, was granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations. His father, Yingkui, was a Remonstrator. His mother was née Dong, and his stepmothers were née Mu and née Lü. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yu, a metropolitan graduate of the same examination cohort, and Ci, Han, Ren, Yi, Gan, Ken, Xian, Ping, and Zong. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twentieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Zequan 俞則全 was registered in a civilian household in Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zuxiu and ranked eleventh in his family. He was twenty-six, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Shuguang, held honorary official status for longevity. His grandfather, Zhenying, held the prestige title Grand Master for Government Service and served as Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Seals. His father, Chaogun, held seventh-rank titular status, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zelian, and his younger brothers were Zezheng and Zejia. He married a woman née Lü. He placed seventy-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Hong, registered in Xingyang County, Zhengzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingzhong; he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather, Zhi, was a National University student; his father was Kongjia, and his mother was née Chu. His mother was living, and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Nian, Fu, and Rui (annotated “born early” [?]). He married a woman née Li. He placed eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Ge, registered in Jishan County, Jiangzhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a Confucian scholar household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Junzheng; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Dong; his grandfather, Zhu, was a Police Chief; his father, Pu, was a Right Chief Administrator; and his mother was née Yao. His mother was living, and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xiang, an education official, and Jia. He married a woman née Hao. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yuan, registered in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziwan; he ranked twenty-eighth in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the intercalary seventh month. His great-grandfather, Wei, received the honorary title of Secretary; his grandfather, Qi, was an Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father, Guang, was a National University student; and his mother was née Ni. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tang, a National University student; Qi, an Administration Vice Commissioner; Shan; Tian (㙉) [?]; Zhang; Leng; Yin, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year (1526); Bang, an Instructor; and Jiong, a National University student. His younger brothers were Di, Lu, Chi, Ying, and Zheng. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Gun, registered in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Gongbu; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-nine, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Shou, was a Clerk; his grandfather was Qian; his father, Zong, was a National University student; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Huang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ren Wanli, registered in a military household in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a prefectural government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Tunan; he ranked first in his family and was thirty years old, born on the seventeenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather, Luan, was a Station Master; his father was Han, and his mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Baili, Yili, and Zhaoli, and his wife was née Han. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ce 陳策, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shixie; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the eleventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hongyu; his grandfather was Rude; his father, Qi, was a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Gu. His parents and grandparents were still living. His younger brother was Ce 筞, and his wife was née Ke. He placed forty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shiyi, registered in a military household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Deyu; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bogang; his grandfather, Wenheng, was a Department Magistrate; his father was Ming, and his mother was née Shi. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Guo, his younger brother was Tang, and his wife was née Lin. He placed forty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wenjin, registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Xianzhi; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Hong, was a Station Master. His grandfather, Yuanjie, was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Upholding Rectitude and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Bang, held those same titles. His mother, née Jiang, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability, and his stepmother, née Ma, was granted that title. His father and stepmother were still living. His elder brothers were Wenshu, Wensui, and Wentong; his younger brothers were Wenmai and Wenyu; and his wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王應期〔貫山西平陽府蒲州，民籍，州學生，治易經，字伯起，行二，年三十四，五月初四日生〕。曾祖鈺，祖源〔壽官〕，父政，母沈氏。重慶下，兄應先，弟應詔、應聘、應試，娶田氏，繼娶蕭氏。山西鄉試第一名，會試第二百七十一名。
translation_en:
Shen Pan, courtesy name Daxin, was from Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was thirteenth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the eleventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xiaoming; his grandfather, Wen; his father, Song; and his mother, née He. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Nian, an official awaiting selection for appointment; Qian, a Steward of a princely household identified as Jipin [?]; Yu, an Assistant Instructor [?]; Gai; Tang, a tribute student; Pi (𡌨, reading uncertain) [?], an official awaiting selection for appointment; and Quan, a Gentleman for Attending Service. His younger brothers were Zheng, Yong, and Luan. His wife was née Wu. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Xing, courtesy name Dingfu, was from Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Guan; his grandfather, Hao; his father, Li; his mother, née Qian; and his stepmother, née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chen, Yi, Ke, and Xian; his younger brothers were Shen, Kun, Zao, Qing, and Kuang. His wife was née Du; he subsequently married a woman née Duan. He placed twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 303rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Cong, courtesy name Shizhen, was from Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was eighth in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jiugao; his grandfather, Gongchao; his father, Wei; and his mother, née You. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Li, Yuan, and Min. His wife was née Hu. He placed eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yingqi, courtesy name Boqi, was from Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, and registered in a civilian household. A department school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Yuan, who held honorary official status in recognition of longevity; his father, Zheng; and his mother, née Shen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Yingxian; his younger brothers were Yingzhao, Yingpin, and Yingshi. His wife was née Tian; he subsequently married a woman née Xiao. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

徐祚，貫忠義後衛官籍，直隸宣城縣人，國子生，治書經，字子厚，行三，年三十一，正月初五日生。曾祖敏〔百戶〕，祖麟〔百戶〕，父永昌〔百戶〕，母倪氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，兄祿〔百戶〕、祐，娶沈氏，繼娶郝氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十名，會試第二百八十九名。

李東光，貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字晋卿，行一，年三十，九月十六日生。曾祖文忠，祖廷祥〔壽官〕，父璽，母殷氏。慈侍下，弟東晨，娶張氏。江西鄉試第五十名，會試第一百三名。
translation_en:
Chen Fei, registered in an artisan household in Yanling County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ruzhong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongqing (an honorary official for longevity); his grandfather was Quan (honorarily appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue); his father was Pu (Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Constitutional Service); and his mother was née Zhao (granted the title Lady of Peace). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were You, Ju, and Gai (all Imperial University students). He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yongming, registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a prefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongcheng; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wu; his grandfather, Qiong; his father, Jie; and his mother, née Shi. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Yongzhong, Yong’en, Yongxiu (a government school student), and Yonghui. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zuo, registered in an officer household of the Zhongyi Rear Guard and a native of Xuancheng County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zihou; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min (a Company Commander); his grandfather, Lin (a Company Commander); his father, Yongchang (a Company Commander); and his mother, née Ni (granted the title Lady of Peace). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lu (a Company Commander) and You. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Hao. He placed one hundred twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dongguang, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jinqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhong; his grandfather, Tingxiang (an honorary official for longevity); his father, Xi; and his mother, née Yin. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brother was Dongchen. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fiftieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lu Ziming was registered in a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was a county-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Dongqing; he ranked third in family order and was thirty-one years old, born on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Changzuo, his grandfather Lun, and his father Jie, a School Instructor. His father’s former wife was née Deng, and his mother was née Fan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Shi, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under the applicable regulations, and Fen. He married a woman née Shi and subsequently a woman née Xie. He placed 135th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 38th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Bo was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a county-school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenshu; he ranked thirty-fourth in family order and was thirty-six years old, born on the nineteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs; his grandfather was Qi, and his father Han, a Clerk. His legal mother was née Xu, and his birth mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mo, Zi, Shi, Zhen, Shu, and Wu; his younger brothers were Chun, Shu, Lin, Qing, Lai, and Mu [the division of the final names is uncertain: ?]. He married a woman née Hua and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed 56th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Yingzhao was registered in a civilian household in Nanzheng County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a prefectural-school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Qiyan; he ranked fifth in family order and was thirty years old, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingzhao, his grandfather Wang, an honorary official in recognition of longevity, and his father Youjue, a Registrar. His mother was née Yang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Yinggao. He married a woman née Chen. He placed 38th in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Sui was registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an added-quota student at the county school, specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Liangqing; he ranked eighth in family order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mou, his grandfather Fu, and his father Bihe; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yao, Xun, and Lin; his younger brothers were Dai, Gou, Di, Tu, and Feng. He married a woman née Tang. He placed 38th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖十四年進士登科錄
text:

山西鄉試第三名會試第一百二十八名

曾祖有才　祖泰　父鼒　母蕭氏
慈侍下　娶楊氏
山東鄉試第二十九名　會試第一百二十四名
punctuated:
吳嘉會〔貫山西振武衛軍籍，湖廣湘陰縣人，代州學生，治書經，字惟禮，行八，年二十四，三月十七日生〕。曾祖貞，祖寧，父琇，母王氏。具慶下，兄嘉聰〔按察司副使〕、嘉善〔監生〕、嘉謨、嘉猷、嘉言，弟嘉禄、嘉亨、嘉徵、嘉章、嘉賓。娶張氏，繼娶席氏。山西鄉試第三名，會試第一百二十八名。

張元〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣官籍，縣學生，治易經，字以貞，行一，年二十八，三月十三日生〕。曾祖偉〔贈刑部主事〕，祖穜〔刑部員外郎〕，父遷，母蘇氏。重慶下，弟孟元、仲元、啓元、繼元、翊元、亮元、秉元、復元、律元、應元、泰元。娶龔氏。浙江鄉試第十四名，會試第二百三十一名。

魏希佐〔貫山東濟南府歷城縣人，國子生，治書經，字以道，行一，年三十四，五月二十六日生〕。曾祖聰，祖鑑〔引禮舍人〕，父武，母黃氏。具慶下，娶牛氏。山東鄉試第七十名，會試第一百八十五名。

王希賢〔貫山東濟南府濟陽縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字行復，行一，年四十二，十二月十五日生〕。曾祖有才，祖泰，父肅，母蕭氏。慈侍下，娶楊氏。山東鄉試第二十九名，會試第一百二十四名。
translation_en:
Wu Jiahui, courtesy name Weili, was registered in a military household of Zhenwu Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Xiangyin County, Huguang. A student of the Daizhou school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was eighth in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the seventeenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Ning, his father Xiu, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiacong, Vice Commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission; Jiashan, an Imperial University student; Jiamo; Jiayou; and Jiayan. His younger brothers were Jialu, Jiaheng, Jiazheng, Jiazhang, and Jiabin. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Xi. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yuan, courtesy name Yizhen, was registered in an official household of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the thirteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Wei, posthumously awarded the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Tong, Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Qian, and his mother née Su. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Mengyuan, Zhongyuan, Qiyuan, Jiyuan, Yiyuan, Liangyuan, Bingyuan, Fuyuan, Lüyuan, Yingyuan, and Taiyuan. He married a woman née Gong. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Xizuo, courtesy name Yidao, was a native of Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Jian, a Ceremonial Usher, his father Wu, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Niu. He placed seventieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xixian, courtesy name Xingfu, was registered in a military household of Jiyang County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Youcai, his grandfather Tai, his father Su, and his mother née Xiao. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖十四年進士登科錄

重慶下兄世昭〔博士〕世竒世經世美娶陳氏繼聘鄧氏
福建鄉試第三十二名會試第一百十九名
===

===
胡叔元
貫陝西西安府咸寧縣民籍應天府溧陽縣〔縣學附學生〕
治易經字允卿行一年二十二四月十九日生
曾祖璉〔封戶部主事累贈通議大夫兵部左侍郎〕　祖汝楫〔進士知縣〕　父佑　母俞氏

陝西鄉試第四十三名　會試第一百三十五名
黃文炳
貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍　國子生
治書經字以約行十年四十三九月十四日生
曾祖弘琋　祖宗信　父敬甫　母張氏
重慶下　兄景欽景誠懋恩〔知縣〕弟文蔚文範　娶林氏

punctuated:
陳中，貫湖廣承天府沔陽州，軍匠籍，州學生，治詩經，字時仲，行一，年三十五，四月三十日生。曾祖讓，祖斌，父紳〔教諭〕，母葉氏，繼母蕭氏。具慶下，弟章、卓，娶司氏。湖廣鄉試第二十名，會試第二百五十四名。

廖世魁，貫福建福州府懷安縣，匠籍，縣學生，治易經，字師文，行六，年三十七，十月十六日生。曾祖法，祖華，父肅，母葉氏。重慶下，兄世昭〔博士〕、世竒、世經、世美，娶陳氏，繼聘鄧氏。福建鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百十九名。

胡叔元，貫陝西西安府咸寧縣，民籍，應天府溧陽縣人，縣學附學生，治易經，字允卿，行一，年二十二，四月十九日生。曾祖璉〔封戶部主事，累贈通議大夫、兵部左侍郎〕，祖汝楫〔進士，知縣〕，父佑，母俞氏。重慶下，弟叔丙、叔才、叔辰、叔辛、叔午、叔戊、叔酉、叔寅、叔羽、叔因、叔九、叔登、叔晋、叔著，娶王氏。陝西鄉試第四十三名，會試第一百三十五名。

黃文炳，貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字以約，行十，年四十三，九月十四日生。曾祖弘珎，祖宗信，父敬甫，母張氏。重慶下，兄景欽、景誠、懋恩〔知縣〕，弟文蔚、文範，娶林氏。福建鄉試第八名，會試第一百六十四名。
translation_en:
Chen Zhong, registered in a military artisan household in Mianyang Subprefecture, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shizhong; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the thirtieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Bin, and his father Shen 〔Instructor〕; his mother was née Ye and his stepmother née Xiao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhang and Zhuo, and his wife was née Si. He placed twentieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Shikui, registered in an artisan household in Huai’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Shiwen; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fa, his grandfather Hua, his father Su, and his mother née Ye. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Shizhao 〔Erudite〕, Shiqi, Shijing, and Shimei. His wife was née Chen; he subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Deng. He placed thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Shuyuan, registered in a commoner household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and a native of Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-two years old, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian 〔honorarily appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and successively granted posthumous titles culminating in Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of War〕; his grandfather was Ruji 〔metropolitan graduate (jinshi) and District Magistrate〕; his father was You and his mother née Yu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Shubing, Shucai, Shuchen, Shuxin, Shuwu (叔午), Shuwu (叔戊), Shuyou, Shuyin, Shuyu, Shuyin (叔因), Shujiu, Shudeng, Shujin, and Shuzhu. His wife was née Wang. He placed forty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Wenbing, registered in a commoner household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Yiyue; he ranked tenth among his brothers and was forty-three years old, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hongzhen, his grandfather Zongxin, his father Jingfu, and his mother née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Jingqin, Jingcheng, and Mao’en 〔District Magistrate〕, and his younger brothers were Wenwei and Wenfan. His wife was née Lin. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖十四年進士登科錄
text:
李世芳〔貫山西潞安府黎城縣軍籍縣學生治詩經字伯傳行一年三十一正月十五日生〕
曾祖浩祖英父謙母劉氏
具慶下弟世蕃世菁世蓁娶王氏繼娶韓氏

===

punctuated:
李世芳〔貫山西潞安府黎城縣軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字伯傳，行一，年三十一，正月十五日生。〕曾祖浩，祖英，父謙，母劉氏。具慶下，弟世蕃、世菁、世蓁。娶王氏，繼娶韓氏。山西鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百六名。

張纓〔貫河南彰德府安陽縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字重卿，行三，年二十八，三月初一日生。〕曾祖時〔主簿〕，祖澤，父瑨，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄纁、紹。娶劉氏。河南鄉試第七十三名，會試第三百十名。

李秉仁〔貫河南汝州寶豐縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字子元，行七，年三十五，七月十七日生。〕曾祖顯質，祖信，父真，前母樊氏，母左氏。慈侍下，兄滄〔監生〕、洪、洙、瀛〔同知〕、濟、濬。娶王氏。河南鄉試第三十四名，會試第一百五十一名。

鄭有周〔貫廣東潮州府揭陽縣民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字郁之，行三，年三十，十一月十五日生。〕曾祖進，祖逢貴，父瑄，母陳氏，繼母許氏。具慶下，兄有禎，弟有宋、有儀、有章、有學、有守。娶薛氏。廣東鄉試第二十四名，會試第二百三十七名。
translation_en:
Li Shifang, registered in a military household in Licheng County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Bochuan; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Ying, his father Qian, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shifan, Shijing, and Shizhen. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Han. He placed thirty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ying, registered in a civilian household in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Chongqing; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi, a Registrar; his grandfather was Ze, his father Jin, and his mother née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xun and Shao. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 310th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bingren, registered in a civilian household in Baofeng County, Ruzhou, Henan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyuan; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianzhi, his grandfather Xin, and his father Zhen; his father’s former wife was née Fan, and his mother was née Zuo. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Cang, an Imperial University student; Hong; Zhu; Ying, an Associate Prefect; Ji; and Jun. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Youzhou, registered in a civilian household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an supplementary student at the county school, specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuzhi; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Fenggui, his father Xuan, his mother née Chen, and his stepmother née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Youzhen, and his younger brothers were Yousong, Youyi, Youzhang, Youxue, and Youshou. He married a woman née Xue. He placed twenty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Weibai, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an supplementary student of the Sanshui County School. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Qiaozhong. He ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-five sui, and was born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Fang, and his father Yingchu; his father's former wife was née Lu, and his mother was née Feng. His parents and members of the grandparental generation were living. His younger brothers were Weichun, Weidou, Weitong, Weizhang, Weikui, Weiyue, Weisong, Weike, Weixiang, Weigou, Weiyi, Weiya, Weiying, Weiyan, Weisong, and Weijing. His wife was née Lao. He placed seventy-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Lianggui, registered in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shimeng. He ranked ninth among his brothers, was thirty-three sui, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhonghong; his grandfather Mo was a County Magistrate, posthumously granted the rank of Gentleman for Attendance; his father Qi was Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Fujian. His mother, née Xiong, was granted the title of Ruren (Lady). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Liangzuo, a titular official, and Liangfu, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dengyun, registered in Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zijian. He ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-seven sui, and was born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Quan, and his father Yan; his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother Chengyun was a Messenger; his younger brothers were Lingyun, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Piyun, Wangyun, Qingyun, and Canyun. His wife was née Chu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Tingmian, registered in Wenshui County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jiwen. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was thirty-nine sui, and was born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenbin; his grandfather Jian held honorary official status for charitable contributions; his father Tao was a Clerk. His mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tinggui, an education official, Tinglu, a County Vice Magistrate, and Tingguan. His wife was née Kang. He placed fifty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Rao Tianmin 饒天民, courtesy name Mingxian, was registered in a military household in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiheng, his grandfather Yu, and his father Bohu; his father’s former wife was née Liu, his mother née Wang, and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tianjue and Tianke, and his wife was née Chen. He placed seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Zongzhe 盧宗哲, courtesy name Junqing, was registered in a military household of the Dezhou Left Guard in Zhili and was a native of Laishui County, Baoding Prefecture. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was De, his grandfather Xin (an honorary official recognized for longevity), and his father Jing; his mother was née Cui and his stepmother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zongru and Zongxian, and his wife was née Tan. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Zhi 胡植, courtesy name Lizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Poetry, he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen, his grandfather Zi, and his father Yuan; his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brothers were Bing, Bang, and Shi, and his wife was née Xiong. He placed sixty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Bangxiu 陳邦脩, courtesy name Deqing, was registered in a civilian household in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked twenty-sixth among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu (a tribute scholar, posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Minister of Works), his grandfather Biao (granted the title of Left Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission and posthumously granted that of Right Vice Minister of Works), and his father Ying; his mother was née Guo. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Bangjie (Assistant Prefect), Bangyan (Vice Prefect), Bangcheng (tribute scholar), Bangfu (Vice Prefect), Bangzhan (Sacrificial Attendant), Bangyou (tribute scholar), Bangteng 邦儯 [?] (a student admitted by virtue of official family status), Bangkan (Secretary in the Ministry of Rites), Bangwo (Registrar in the Chief Military Commission of the Rear), and Bangjian (Vice Commissioner of a Salt Distribution Commission). His wife was née Li. He placed third in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

安宅〔貫山東東昌府冠縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字子仁，行一，年二十五，九月三十日生〕。曾祖甫能，祖宏〔巡檢〕，父世昌，母劉氏。重慶下，弟遴、述，娶許氏。山東鄉試第五名，會試第二百三名。

梅凌雲〔貫江西九江府湖口縣民籍，浙江蘭谿縣教諭，治易經，字尚志，行二，年三十八，閏十一月二十一日生〕。曾祖清〔贈工部主事〕，祖愈〔知府〕，父鳳，母崔氏。慈侍下，兄凌霄，弟凌雪、凌虛、凌寒，娶孫氏。江西鄉試第一百四十六名，會試第九十五名。

張𤦺〔貫山西太原府石州民籍，州學增廣生，治易經，字席玉，行二，年二十四，二月十七日生〕。曾祖大全，祖讓，父文紳〔封監察御史，贈大理寺左少卿〕，嫡母康氏〔贈孺人，加贈恭人〕，繼母馮氏〔封孺人〕，生母崔氏。慈侍下，兄玫、玠、珩〔大理寺左少卿〕、瑋、珊、瓊、璉、珖、肆，娶王氏。山西鄉試第二十六名，會試第三百十五名。

靳學顏〔貫山東兖州府濟寧州民籍，州學生，治易經，字子愚，行一，年二十三，八月十七日生〕。曾祖禮，祖鐘，父顯〔引禮舍人〕，母田氏。重慶下，弟學曾，娶張氏。山東鄉試第一名，會試第一百五十五名。
translation_en:
An Zhai, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in a civilian household in Guan County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Funeng; his grandfather, Hong, was a Police Chief; his father was Shichang, and his mother was née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Lin and Shu, and his wife was née Xu. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mei Lingyun, courtesy name Shangzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Hukou County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. The Instructor of Lanxi County, Zhejiang, he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-first day of the intercalary eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qing, was posthumously granted the title of Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather, Yu, was a Prefect; his father was Feng, and his mother was née Cui. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Lingxiao, and his younger brothers were Lingxue, Lingxu, and Linghan. His wife was née Sun. He placed 146th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qi (張𤦺), courtesy name Xiyu, was registered in a civilian household in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. An added-quota student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the seventeenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daquan; his grandfather was Rang; and his father, Wenshen, was granted the honorary title of Investigating Censor and posthumously granted that of Left Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. His legal mother, née Kang, was posthumously granted the title ruren and subsequently the higher title gongren; his stepmother, née Feng, was granted the title ruren; his birth mother was née Cui. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Mei, Jie, Heng (Left Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review), Wei, Shan, Qiong, Lian, Guang, and Si [?]. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Xueyan, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in a civilian household in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-three years old, born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather was Zhong; his father, Xian, was a Ceremonial Usher; and his mother was née Tian. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Xuezeng, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.
